| RAN1#124 | 9.3.2.1 | Agreement | Update TR 38.769 on SFO calibration<br>\| 6A.1.x.y SFO calibration It is reported by sources [R1-10321-123-1, FUTUREWEI], [R1-10321-123-2, Spreadtrum], [R1-10321-123-3, vivo], [R1-10321-123-6, Huawei], [R1-10321-123-10, CTC], [R1-10321-123-9, CATT], [R1-10321-123-13, Samsung], [R1-10321-123-14, ZTE], [R1-10321-123-26, TCL], [R1-10321-123-24, Qualcomm], [R1-10321-123-25, NTT DOCOMO], and [R1-10321-123-23, Quectel] and [LGE] that SFO calibration is necessary for device 2b. And it is reported by sources [R1-10321-123-1, FUTUREWEI], [R1-10321-123-2, Spreadtrum], [R1-10321-123-6, Huawei], [R1-10321-123-9, CATT], [R1-10321-123-26, TCL], [R1-10321-123-24, Qualcomm], [R1-10321-123-25, NTT DOCOMO], and [R1-10321-123-23, Quectel] and [LGE] that SFO calibration is necessary for device C. The functionality of SFO calibration using the following options is studied: Option 1: CAP defined in TS 38.291 [228] and/or Manchester encoding. - Sources [R1-10321-123-9, CATT], [R1-10321-123-13, Samsung], [R1-10321-123-19, Apple], [R1-10321-123-23, Quectel], and [R1-10321-123-26, TCL], [LGE] and [Ericsson] report that SFO is feasible and can be achieved by reusing CAP. - Sources [R1-10321-123-2, Spreadtrum], [R1-10321-123-6, Huawei], [R1-10321-123-12, OPPO], [R1-10321-123-13, Samsung], [R1-10321-123-14, ZTE], [R1-10321-123-19, Apple], and [R1-10321-123-23, Quectel] [LGE] and [Ericsson] state that the SFO calibration is feasible and can be achieved by Manchester coding for PRDCH. Option 2: A sequence-based SIP. - Sources [R1-10321-123-3, vivo], [R1-10321-123-8, NEC], [R1-10321-123-10, CTC], and [R1-10321-123-14, ZTE] and [LGE] report that SFO calibration is feasible and can be achieved by receiving sequence-based SIP. Option 3: A CFO calibration signal. - Sources [R1-10321-123-1, FUTUREWEI], [R1-10321-123-2, Spreadtrum], [R1-10321-123-6, Huawei], [R1-10321-123-9, CATT], [R1-10321-123-12, OPPO], [R1-10321-123-19, Apple], [R1-10321-123-24, Qualcomm], [R1-10321-123-23, Quectel], [R1-10321-123-30, Sony] and [R1-10321-123-25, NTT DOCOMO] report that SFO calibration is feasible and can be achieved by CFO calibration signal. Additionally, source [R1-10321-123-6, Huawei] state that this method applies to device C. \| | [Chair notes RAN1#124 - eom_03](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124%20-%20eom_03.docx)<br>[R1-2600487](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Docs/R1-2600487.zip) |

| RAN1#124 | 9.3.2.1 | Agreement | For sequence design for periodic synchronization signal, capture the following in TR38.769<br>---<br>Regarding sequence type for periodic synchronization signal<br>- Source [vivo] and [CATT] state, that m sequence can be considered as sequence type for periodic sync signal.<br>- Source [Ericsson] states, a set of unique patterns of the binary sequences can be used for periodic sync signal<br>- Source [Apple] states that, M-sequence with length 31 should be considered as baseline for periodic synchronization signal, with Manchester coding applied for SFO tracking.<br>- Source [Docomo] states that, for sequence type of R2D synchronization signal for frequency synchronization, m sequence or Golay sequence with good auto-correlation property should be considered.<br>- Source [R1-10321-123-6, Huawei] state that the periodic synchronization signal is binary sequence-based, using a Golay sequence with good auto-correlation characteristic and low correlation complexity, with a fixed maximum length, in order to reduce the blind detection effort by the device for the time and frequency synchronization.<br>Regarding sequence length for periodic synchronization signal<br>- Source [vivo] states that, for sequence length of periodic sync sequence, to achieve target coverage for outdoor scenario.<br>  - The m-sequence with length 31 with Manchester coding using M=2, occupied 31 OFDM symbols can be considered for periodic sync sequence, assuming 38 dBm Tx power and 20 dB penetration.<br>  - The m-sequence with length 127 with Manchester coding using M=2, occupied 127 OFDM symbols can be considered for periodic sync sequence, assuming 33 dBm Tx power and 20 dB penetration.<br>- Source [Qualcomm] states that, for R2D synchronization signal (SS), Device 2b requires a longer length than Device C because of its larger initial SFO/CFO.<br>  - For Device C with initial SFO/CFO of 50ppm<br>    - The SS sequence with 7.5 symbols (with 63-length m-sequence and M=2) can achieve MD of 10% at an SNR lower than PRDCH with 20bit+6bit CRC, M=2, TBCC 1/3 (e.g., for R2D L1 control).<br>  - For Device 2b with an initial SFO/CFO of 1000ppm,<br>    - The SS sequence with 31.5 symbols (with 15-length m-sequence and M=2) can achieve MD of 10% at an SNR lower than PRDCH with 20bit+6bit CRC, M=2, TBCC 1/3 (e.g., for R2D L1 control).<br>- Source [R1-10321-123-6, Huawei] state that the periodic synchronization signal should be the maximum length e.g., 256 for the binary sequence to guarantee all the devices with the maximum coverage distance can access the network.<br>Regarding the number of sequences for periodic synchronization signal<br>- Sources [R1-10321-123-3, vivo], [R1-10321-123-5, CMCC], [R1-10321-123-7, Ericsson], [R1-10321-123-9, CATT] and [R1-10321-123-24, Qualcomm] report that a predefined number, e.g., 3~4 sequences can be considered for reader differentiation<br>  - Source [CATT] states that, the reader identification information, which indicates the identifier of the reader, should be carried by R2D synchronization signal. The number of binary sequence(s) of R2D synchronization signal should be equal to 4 for reader identification.<br>  - Source [vivo] states that, it is benificial to consider m-sequence with ~3 sequences for reader differentiation<br>- Sources [R1-10321-123-6, Huawei], [R1-10321-123-8, NEC], [R1-10321-123-5, CMCC] and [R1-10321-123-21, MTK] report that Single sequence can be considered.<br>  - Source [Huawei] further state that if multiple sequences of the periodic synchronization signal are used, it will increase the complexity and power consumption of the device.<br>- Source [ZTE] states that, the blind decoding using multiple 8-length sequences has ~2dB performance loss compared with single-sequence detection. The necessity of synchronization signal with multiple sequences needs to be discussed.<br>- Source [Docomo] states that, for the number of sequences of R2D synchronization signal for frequency synchronization, device complexity on correlation-based detection should be considered assuming that device performs correlation-based detection to detect the signal on multiple candidate frequencies at least for initial frequency acquisition.<br>--- | [Chair notes RAN1#124 - eom_03](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124%20-%20eom_03.docx)<br>[R1-2600488](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Docs/R1-2600488.zip) |
| RAN1#124 | 9.3.2.1 | Agreement | Update TR 38.769 on how the L1 R2D control information is transmitted<br>\| 6A.1.x.4 FEC and repetition Regarding FEC and repetition for L1 R2D control part, sources [R1-10321-123-3, vivo], [R1-10321-123-12, OPPO], [R1-10321-123-5, CMCC], [R1-10321-123-1, FUTUREWEI], [R1-10321-123-8, NEC], [R1-10321-123-9, CATT], [R1-10321-123-10, CTC], [R1-10321-123-14, ZTE], and [R1-10321-123-24, Qualcomm], and [Huawei] report that FEC and repetition can also be applied to L1 R2D control information. Source [R1-10321-123-6, Huawei] state that repetition is needed for L1 R2D control information. Source [R1-10321-123-1, FUTUREWEI] and [R1-10321-123-9, CATT] report that FEC can be applied to L1 R2D control information. Sources [R1-10321-123-3, vivo], [R1-10321-123-5, CMCC], [R1-10321-123-8, NEC], [R1-10321-123-12, OPPO], [R1-10321-123-10, CTC], [R1-10321-123-14, ZTE] and [R1-10321-123-24, Qualcomm] report methods to determine FEC, repetition related parameters for L1 R2D control information, if FEC/repetition is supported for L1 control. - Sources [R1-10321-123-3, vivo], [R1-10321-123-5, CMCC], [R1-10321-123-8, NEC], [R1-10321-123-14, ZTE] and [R1-10321-123-24, Qualcomm] report that the parameters for repetition and FEC for L1 R2D control information can be pre-configured, e.g., by broadcast information. [R1-10321-123-12, OPPO] report that these parameters should be pre-known by device. - Sources [R1-10321-123-8, NEC] and [R1-10321-123-10, CTC] states that parameters for repetition and FEC for L1 R2D control information can be fixed and pre-defined. Source [R1-10321-123-8, NEC] also state that these parameters can be indicated by a set of different binary sequences with fixed or variable length for indication. Source [R1-10321-123-8, NEC] report that a separate interleaving is needed for L1 R2D control. - Source [Huawei] state that The FEC and repetition parameters of the L1 R2D control information of the SIB-like broadcast information is predefined or indicated by the MIB-like broadcast information. The FEC and repetition parameters of the L1 R2D control information after the SIB-like broadcast information is indicated by the SIB-like broadcast information. 6A.1.x.5 Payload size of control Sources [R1-10321-123-3, vivo], [R1-10321-123-12, OPPO], [R1-10321-123-7, Ericsson], and [R1-10321-123-19, Apple], and [LGE] report that device only detects one payload size at a given time. And [R1-10321-123-3, vivo] also report that up to two payload sizes can be considered and detected by preamble. Source [Qualcomm] state that two different sizes for L1 control can be considered for unicast and non-unicast. Source [Xiaomi] states that only one payload size for L1 control information should be considered to reduce the reception complexity. Source [Huawei] state that the size of the L1 control information is 10~12 bits considering at least the FEC code rate, repetition number and TBS. Source [Samsung] state that R2D L1 control information is variable, and within 24 bits for 6-bit CRC attachment. Source [ZTE] state that L1 control occupies one or multiple full OFDM symbols. [Omit unchanged part] 6A.1.x.7 CRC R2D control information with a separate CRC from data is studied. Source [R1-10321-123-1, FUTUREWEI] states that, for separate CRC on the L1 R2D control information, when the size of the L1 R2D control information is 24 bits or less, the existing CRC6 specification can be reused, if the size of the L1 R2D control information is between 25 and 57 bits, the existing CRC6 polynomial can be reused without impact to the undetected error rate. Sources [R1-10321-123-11, Xiaomi], and [R1-10321-123-19, Apple], [Huawei] and [LGE] state that how to attach the separate CRC for L1 R2D control information needs to be considered, and a fixed length (equal to or larger than 16) of CRC is required to ensure the reliability and avoid unnecessary blind detection for L1 R2D control information. Source [Ericsson], [vivo], [Qualcomm] and [TCL] suggest to use the same rule as R19, 6 bits for < 25 TBS and 16 bits otherwise. Source [vivo] state that this provides sufficient CRC protection and reasonable overhead. Source [Samsung] suggest to always use 6 bits, assuming no larger than 24 bits payload for L1 control information. \| | [Chair notes RAN1#124 - eom_03](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124%20-%20eom_03.docx)<br>[R1-2600488](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Docs/R1-2600488.zip) |
| RAN1#124 | 9.3.2.1 | Agreement | Update TR 38.768 on whether L1 R2D control information and data payload of PRDCH are contiguous in time<br>\| 6A.1.x.2 Time location L1 control information precedes the data payload of the PRDCH. Option 1: L1 R2D control information and data payload of PRDCH are contiguous in time. - Sources [R1-10321-123-13 Samsung] and [R1-10321-123-19, Apple] state that, transmit L1 R2D control information and data payload in the same PRDCH with contiguous time resources and same frequency resource is beneficial for low device complexity. [R1-10321-123-19, Apple] further report that this simplifies the timeline design. - Sources [R1-10321-123-3, vivo] and [R1-10321-123-8, NEC] report that the time gap is not long enough to introduce gap between L1 R2D control information and data payload. Sources [R1-10321-123-6, Huawei], [R1-10321-123-8, NEC] further states that decoding of L1 R2D control information the device can parallelly store the data payload in buffer, and receive L1 R2D control information, hence time gap is not needed. Source [vivo] provide the analysis with reference show that the decoding latency of L1 control signaling (assuming ~30bits payload size) is a few tens of us, less than one OFDM symbol. The memory required for buffer signal during one OFDM symbol is limited(~2000bits), and feasible even for passive device, according to product datasheet, and also feasible for active device. - Sources [R1-10321-123-3, vivo], and [R1-10321-123-14, ZTE], [Spreadtrum] and [CATT] report that L1 R2D control transmitted in the same frequency as data payload in PRDCH, and time gap is not needed. - Source [R1-10321-123-16, LGE] report that no time gap needed if the chip length for L1 R2D control information is the same as that for data payload of PRDCH. Source [vivo] state that different chip length for L1 control and data part does not require clock rate change. Option 2: L1 R2D control information and data payload of PRDCH are not contiguous in time. - Sources [R1-10321-123-1, FUTUREWEI], [R1-10321-123-7, Ericsson] and [R1-10321-123-11, Xiaomi] report that a short time gap is needed if the device is not capable of decoding L1 R2D control and buffering data payload of PRDCH. - Source [R1-10321-123-5, CMCC] state that, L1 R2D control and data payload are transmitted in separated physical channel, hence they are not contiguous. - Source [R1-10321-123-12, OPPO] state that, time gap is needed to switch the frequency if L1 R2D control is transmitted in different frequency from data payload. - Source [R1-10321-123-1, FUTUREWEI], [R1-10321-123-16] report that time gap maybe needed if the chip length for L1 R2D control information is different from that for data payload of PRDCH. - Source [R1-10321-123-24, Qualcomm] report that, if there is a gap, midamble can be inserted between L1 R2D control information and data payload. - Source [interDigital] and [Quectel] time gap is needed for flexibility for R2D data payload transmission in time. Factors affecting the choice between the above options were reported as follows: - Whether device buffers data part before finishing L1 control decoding, as reported by sources [R1-10321-123-3, vivo], [R1-10321-123-6, Huawei], [R1-10321-123-13, Samsung], [R1-10321-123-2, Spreadtrum], [R1-10321-123-25, NTT DOCOMO], [R1-10321-123-5, CMCC], [R1-10321-123-12, OPPO], [R1-10321-123-7, Ericsson], [R1-10321-123-24, Qualcomm], [R1-10321-123-8, NEC], [R1-10321-123-4, Nokia], [R1-10321-123-11, Xiaomi], [R1-10321-123-14, ZTE] and [R1-10321-123-19, Apple]. - Sources [R1-10321-123-3, vivo], [R1-10321-123-6, Huawei], [R1-10321-123-13, Samsung], [R1-10321-123-2, Spreadtrum], [R1-10321-123-25, NTT DOCOMO], [R1-10321-123-8, NEC] and [R1-10321-123-14, ZTE] state that gap between L1 R2D control and data is not needed, assuming device can buffer data part before finishing L1 R2D control decoding. Source [R1-10321-123-6, Huawei] further state that the time gap would increase the power consumption of the device. - Sources [R1-10321-123-5, CMCC], [R1-10321-123-12, OPPO], and [R1-10321-123-11, Xiaomi], [Nokia], [interDigital], [Sony] and [Quectel] state that time gap is needed to reduce/avoid buffer at AIoT device. - Whether frequency resource is different for L1 R2D control information and data payload, as reported by sources [R1-10321-123-12, OPPO], and [R1-10321-123-4, Nokia], and [Quectel]. - Whether chip duration (M value) is different for L1 R2D control information and data payload, which is reported by sources [R1-10321-123-1, FUTUREWEI], [R1-10321-123-6, Huawei] and [R1-10321-123-16, LGE ] - Whether L1 R2D control information and data payload are separate channel, as reported by source [R1-10321-123-5, CMCC] - Whether CFO calibration signal is placed between L1 R2D control information and data payload, as reported by [R1-10321-123-18, Lenovo]. - Whether flexibility for time location for PRDCH data payload in relation to L1 R2D control information is necessary, as reported by [R1-10321-123-18, Lenovo], [vivo], [interDigital] and [Quectel]. \| | [Chair notes RAN1#124 - eom_03](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124%20-%20eom_03.docx)<br>[R1-2600488](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Docs/R1-2600488.zip) |
| RAN1#124 | 9.3.2.1 | Agreement | Update TR 38.769 for whether L1 control and data payload is transmitted in the same PRDCH, or Separate PRDCH.<br>\| 6A.1.x.6 Physical channel No new R2D physical channel for L1 R2D control information is introduced. Sources [R1-10321-123-3, vivo], [R1-10321-123-24, Qualcomm], [R1-10321-123-6, Huawei], [R1-10321-123-13, Samsung], [R1-10321-123-1, FUTUREWEI], [R1-10321-123-25, NTT DOCOMO], [R1-10321-123-8, NEC], [R1-10321-123-16, LGE ], [R1-10321-123-19, Apple], and [R1-10321-123-20, InterDigital] and [Spreadtrum]state that L1 R2D control is transmitted in the same PRDCH carries data payload for simplicity for standard and device. - [R1-10321-123-6, Huawei] states if L1 control and data are in different PRDCH, the time relationship design is complicated and the device needs to buffer the L1 control information for a long time which is hard for the device to implement. - Source [NEC] state that the coding/repetition scheme for the control information is like the data payload, and also no specific reference RS would be dedicatedly introduced for the control information. Sources [R1-10321-123-14, ZTE], [R1-10321-123-5, CMCC], [R1-10321-123-15, Transsion], [R1-10321-123-17, Panasonic], and [R1-10321-123-21, MediaTek] and [Xiaomi] state that L1 R2D control information is transmitted in a separate PRDCH - Source [R1-10321-123-14] report that, L1 R2D control information is encoded separately, it is more appropriate to transmit L1 R2D control information on a separate PRDCH - Sources [R1-10321-123-5, CMCC] and [R1-10321-123-15, Transsion] state that, defining a new PRDCH format to carry L1 R2D control information only is more efficient for scheduling and resource utilization. - Source [R1-10321-123-17, Panasonic] state that, L1 control information is transmitted in separated PRDCH since control part would require higher reliability, and one control information could be used for multiple PRDCH transmissions. - Source [Xiaomi] state that separated transmission should be adopted if option 2(non-contiguous) for time location of L1 R2D control information and R2D data payload. \| | [Chair notes RAN1#124 - eom_03](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124%20-%20eom_03.docx)<br>[R1-2600488](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Docs/R1-2600488.zip) |
| RAN1#124 | 9.3.2.1 | Agreement | Update TR38.769 on chip duration determination for data payload<br>\| 6A.1.x.y.1 Chip duration of data payload The chip duration determination of the data payload in the PRDCH and the L1 control information are studied. The following options are studied for the functionality of the chip duration determination of the data payload in the PRDCH: Option 1-data: The chip duration of the corresponding L1 R2D control information is used. [omit unchanged part] Option 2-data: The chip duration indicated by the corresponding L1 R2D control information is used. - Sources [R1-10321-123-1, FUTUREWEI], [R1-10321-123-3, vivo], [R1-10321-123-5, CMCC], [R1-10321-123-7, Ericsson], [R1-10321-123-8, NEC], [R1-10321-123-10, CTC], [R1-10321-123-11, Xiaomi], [R1-10321-123-14, ZTE], [R1-10321-123-16, LGE ], [R1-10321-123-17, Panasonic],[R1-10321-123-25, NTT DOCOMO], [R1-10321-123-19, Apple], [R1-10321-123-24, Qualcomm], and [R1-10321-123-28, CEWiT], and [CATT] report that, chip duration of the data payload in the PRDCH indicated by the corresponding L1 R2D control information, have the following benefits: [omit unchanged part] - Sources [R1-10321-123-19, Apple] and [R1-10321-123-7, Ericsson] state that this option provides flexibility to adapt to different coverage conditions or message types, with [R1-10321-123-7, Ericsson] states this option provides benefits for PRDCH like Msg2 and Msg4. Source [ZTE] state that the chip duration of an R2D data payload without L1 control (if supported), if present, is a fixed value. \| | [Chair notes RAN1#124 - eom_03](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124%20-%20eom_03.docx)<br>[R1-2600488](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Docs/R1-2600488.zip) |
| RAN1#124 | 9.3.2.1 | Agreement | Update TR 38.769 for content in L1 R2D control information.<br>\| 6A.1.x R2D control information 6A.1.x.1 Content In addition to TBS for PRDCH data payload, the following L1 R2D control information, which potentially can be indicated to the device, is studied: - M value for PRDCH data payload chip duration, as reported by [R1-10321-123-3, vivo], [R1-10321-123-24, Qualcomm], [R1-10321-123-5, CMCC], [R1-10321-123-12, OPPO], [R1-10321-123-1, FUTUREWEI], [R1-10321-123-7, Ericsson], [R1-10321-123-25, NTT DOCOMO], [R1-10321-123-4, Nokia], [R1-10321-123-8, NEC], [R1-10321-123-9, CATT], [R1-10321-123-10, CTC], [R1-10321-123-11, Xiaomi], [R1-10321-123-14, ZTE], [R1-10321-123-15, Transsion], [R1-10321-123-16, LGE ], [R1-10321-123-17, Panasonic], [R1-10321-123-19, Apple], [R1-10321-123-20, InterDigital], [R1-10321-123-26, TCL] and [R1-10321-123-28, CEWiT]. - On the other hand, sources [R1-10321-123-2, Spreadtrum], [R1-10321-123-6, Huawei], [R1-10321-123-7, Ericsson] and [R1-10321-123-29, Sequans] suggest to use same chip duration between L1 R2D control information and data payload, hence M value indication is not needed in L1 R2D control. - Repetition/FEC related parameters for PRDCH data payload, as reported by sources [R1-10321-123-3, vivo], [R1-10321-123-24, Qualcomm], [R1-10321-123-6, Huawei], [R1-10321-123-5, CMCC], [R1-10321-123-12, OPPO], [R1-10321-123-1, FUTUREWEI], [R1-10321-123-2, Spreadtrum], [R1-10321-123-7, Ericsson], [R1-10321-123-25, NTT DOCOMO], [R1-10321-123-8, NEC], [R1-10321-123-9, CATT], [R1-10321-123-10, CTC], [R1-10321-123-14, ZTE], [R1-10321-123-15, Transsion], [R1-10321-123-16, LGE ], [R1-10321-123-19, Apple], [R1-10321-123-20, InterDigital], [R1-10321-123-26, TCL], and [R1-10321-123-28, CEWiT], and [Quectel], if Repetition/FEC is supported for R2D. - Timing related information for PRDCH data payload, as reported by sources [R1-10321-123-24, Qualcomm], [R1-10321-123-5, CMCC], [R1-10321-123-12, OPPO], [R1-10321-123-4, Nokia], [R1-10321-123-15, Transsion], [R1-10321-123-16, LGE ], [R1-10321-123-20, InterDigital] and [R1-10321-123-28, CEWiT], considering potential need of gap between L1 R2D control and corresponding data payload. - On the other hand, sources [R1-10321-123-3, vivo], [R1-10321-123-6, Huawei], [R1-10321-123-13, Samsung], [R1-10321-123-2, Spreadtrum], [R1-10321-123-25, NTT DOCOMO], [R1-10321-123-8, NEC] and [R1-10321-123-14, ZTE] state that, this information is not included in L1 R2D control, because of no need of gap between L1 R2D control and corresponding data payload. - Timing gap between R2D and the corresponding D2R transmission, as reported by [R1-10321-123-24, Qualcomm] - Frequency resource for PRDCH data payload, as reported by sources [R1-10321-123-7, Ericsson], [R1-10321-123-23, Quectel] and [R1-10321-123-28, CEWiT], if FDM for R2D is supported. - Message types/Functional indication, as reported by Sources [R1-10321-123-24, Qualcomm], [R1-10321-123-3, vivo], [R1-10321-123-12, OPPO], [R1-10321-123-13, Samsung], [R1-10321-123-1, FUTUREWEI], [R1-10321-123-4, Nokia], [R1-10321-123-11, Xiaomi], [R1-10321-123-14, ZTE] and [R1-10321-123-5, CMCC], for the purpose of early termination of R2D detection. Source [Qualcomm] state that it can be used to indicate which system information is transmitted. Besides, source [Samsung] state that if message type is included in L1 R2D control information, TBS is not necessary to be explicitly indicated in L1 R2D control information. - ID related information, which potentially include at least one of reader ID, device ID or Transaction ID related information - ID related information associated with device(s) - Sources [R1-10321-123-1, FUTUREWEI], [R1-10321-123-3, vivo], [R1-10321-123-24, Qualcomm], [R1-10321-123-12, OPPO], [R1-10321-123-13, Samsung] and [R1-10321-123-26, TCL] state that, ID related information associated with device(s), indicating for which device or group of devices the upcoming data is intended, can be included in L1 R2D control for early termination. - Reader ID related information, if needed, as reported by source [R1-10321-123-24, Qualcomm]. - Indication of next R2D transmission, as reported by source [R1-10321-123-1, FUTUREWEI], [Quectel] and [Panasonic], used to indicate when the next R2D transmission. Source [R1-10321-123-1, FUTUREWEI] state that the indication can help non-intended devices have the opportunity to harvest energy. Source [Panasonic] states that starting time for PRDCH for multi PRDCH scheduling should be indicated. - D2R resources to send ACK/NACK feedback for unicast R2D command reception, as reported by source [Qualcomm]. - Frequency adjustment information indicated to AIoT device for CFO calibration, as reported by source [vivo]. - Indicator relevant to DO-A access, as reported by source [Nokia]. And Indicator relevant to first D2R of scheduling request for DO-A, as reported by source [Lenovo]. - Indication of round number in access trigger, as reported by [Qualcomm]. \| | [Chair notes RAN1#124 - eom_03](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124%20-%20eom_03.docx)<br>[R1-2600488](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Docs/R1-2600488.zip) |
| RAN1#124 | 9.3.2.1 | Agreement | Capture the following in TR38.769<br>---<br>Regarding the necessity and feasibility on scrambling for PRDCH,<br>[Negative to apply scrambling]<br>- Source [R1-10321-123-3, vivo] states that, it is unnecessary to support scrambling for PRDCH, as interference randomization is limited for OOK modulation with Manchester coding.<br>- Source [R1-10321-123-3, vivo] states that, continuous 1s or 0s cannot be effectively reduced by scrambling, while Manchester coding can guarantee no larger than 2 continuous 1s or 0s and simplify gNB transmission power adjustment. Source [vivo] states that Manchester coding already guarantees no larger than 2 continuous 1s or 0s.<br>- Source [R1-10321-123-6, Huawei] states that, R2D scrambling should not be supported since it cannot work for intra-frequency interference handling as the receiver cannot detect the signals received from multiple readers of the same frequency locations.<br>- Source [R1-10321-123-9, CATT] and [R1-10321-123-11, Xiaomi] state that, for PRDCH, scrambling should not be supported to avoid increasing A-IoT complexity and power consumption.<br>- Source [Xiaomi] states that, the scrambling for PRDCH is unnecessary for interference randomization and continuous 1s or 0s avoidance, and should be deprioritized.<br>[Positive to apply scrambling]<br>- Source [R1-10321-123-12, OPPO], [R1-10321-123-25, Docomo], [R1-10321-123-26, TCL], [R1-10321-123-13, Samsung], [R1-10321-123-24, Qualcomm] and [IITK] state that, scrambling should be applied to R2D transmissions for mitigating interference among R2D transmissions from different readers.<br>- Source [R1-10321-123-24, Qualcomm] states that, it is feasible and necessary to apply PRDCH scrambling for interference randomization and inter-cell interference reduction, especially for dense deployments with frequency reuse. Scrambling sequences can be initialized using parameters like reader ID, device ID or partial ID for PRDCH, which can be implemented efficiently even in constrained devices. The scrambling can be applied to the bits after coding and repetitions.<br>- Source [R1-10321-123-7, Ericsson] states that, R2D scrambling is necessary to reduce inter-cell interference and ensure statistical uniformity, preventing long runs of identical bits and improving clock recovery. R2D scrambling is feasible, requiring only a small LFSR and one XOR per bit , leading to negligible hardware complexity.<br>--- | [Chair notes RAN1#124 - eom_03](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124%20-%20eom_03.docx)<br>[R1-2600488](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Docs/R1-2600488.zip) |
| RAN1#124 | 9.3.2.1 | Agreement | It is feasible to support R2D FEC and block level repetition for R20 AIoT. | [Chair notes RAN1#124 - eom_03](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124%20-%20eom_03.docx)<br>[R1-2600488](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Docs/R1-2600488.zip) |
| RAN1#124 | 9.3.2.1 | Agreement | It is necessary to support R2D FEC and/or block level repetitions for AIoT device in R2D to achieve maximum coverage (e.g., 200 m with penetration loss for Device 2b, 500 m with penetration loss for Device C) as observed in [Refer the TP on Necessity of R2D FEC], and it can be enabled under certain condition.<br>- This does not preclude reader to disable FEC and/or block level repetition. | [Chair notes RAN1#124 - eom_03](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124%20-%20eom_03.docx)<br>[R1-2600488](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Docs/R1-2600488.zip) |
| RAN1#124 | 9.3.2.1 | Agreement | Update TR38.769, on R2D multiplexing, as follows<br>\| FDM for R2D from the same reader is studied, considering the complexity of a device required to support FDM, and how a device determines the frequency resource to receive the FDMed R2D transmissions. In assessing feasibility of such FDM: - Sources [R1-10321-123-1, FUTUREWEI], [R1-10321-123-2, Spreadtrum], [R1-10321-123-6, Huawei, HiSilicon] , [ZTE], [InterDigital (R1-2507754)] and [R1-10321-123-25, NTT DOCOMO] state that R2D FDM is feasible for Device 2b and for Device C, considering device equipped with IF/ZIF filters at the receiver. - Source [R1-10321-123-7, Ericsson] states that the total number of PRBs required to multiplex devices using FDM needs to be defined. Source [Ericsson] further states that if multiplexing UEs using FDM requires a larger transmission bandwidth (ergo channel bandwidth) than in Rel-19, then to minimize the specification impacts, the smallest channel bandwidths available in NR i.e., 3 MHz CBW (15-PRBs) and 5 MHz CBW (25-PRBs) can be considered. - Source [vivo] states when AIoT R2D bandwidth is less than 4 RBs, it is not feasible to support R2D FDM for device 2b with large residual CFO, i.e., 100ppm. [Omit Unchanged part] Regarding how a device determines the frequency resource for receiving one of the FDMed R2D transmissions: - Sources [R1-10321-123-1 FUTUREWEI], [R1-10321-123-6 Huawei, HiSilicon] [R1-10321-123-2 Spreadtrum] and [R1-10321-123-24 Qualcomm] state that the frequency resource of synchronization signal, CFO calibration signal or broadcast information need to be fixed or predefined. - Sources [R1-10321-123-6 Huawei, HiSilicon], [R1-10321-123-2 Spreadtrum], [R1-10321-123-24 Qualcomm], [R1-10321-123-25 NTT DOCOMO], [R1-10321-123-8 NEC], [R1-10321-123-14 ZTE], [Xiaomi] and [R1-10321-123-12 OPPO] state that some of R2D transmissions e.g., L1 control information or a R2D transmission other than sync signal or broadcast information can determine their frequency resources based on the indication. - Source [R1-10321-123-12 OPPO] state that the frequency resource for data payload is indicated by corresponding L1 R2D control. - Source [R1-10321-123-8 NEC] and [R1-10321-123-25 NTT DOCOMO] state that the frequency resource of a R2D transmission can be associated with the previous corresponding D2R transmission. - Source [R1-10321-123-8 NEC] state that the exact frequency resource/channel for a R2D transmission can be associated with a specific coverage level from a set of candidates R2D frequency resources preconfigured. - Source [Sharp] states that a Device 2b or Device C is not required to receive more than one of the FDM’ed R2D transmissions. \| | [Chair notes RAN1#124 - eom_03](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124%20-%20eom_03.docx)<br>[R1-2600488](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Docs/R1-2600488.zip) |
| RAN1#124 | 9.3.2.1 | Agreement | Regarding CP handling for M value larger than or equal to 24, Capture the following in TR 38.769<br>---<br>For CP handling for M value larger than or equal to 24 if supported,<br>[Negative to reuse R19 CP handling method]<br>- Source [vivo], [R1-10321-123-24, Qualcomm], [Honor, R1-2507210] state that, with improved SFO accuracy, special CP handling may not be necessary for all supported values of M.<br>- Source [CATT] states that, if the CP handling does not impact the R2D reception performance, the additional two chips with “ON” would not be needed. In this case, the transmission efficiency would be further improved for R2D transmission in Rel- 20.<br>[Positive to reuse R19 CP handling method or new CP handling method]<br>- Source [R1-10321-123-1, Futurewei] proposes to adopt the same CP handling method used for M=24 to the case of M=32.<br>- Source [R1-10321-123-2, Spreadtrum] states that, for M = 32, CP handling issue should be further considered.<br>- Source [R1-10321-123-16, LGE] states that, Regarding the large M value, additional CP handling solutions may be required. For example, mapping the last N chips (e.g., N = 3 or 4) of the OOK chip part to ON chips could be considered as a potential solution.<br>[End of TP]<br>--- | [Chair notes RAN1#124 - eom_03](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124%20-%20eom_03.docx)<br>[R1-2600489](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Docs/R1-2600489.zip) |
| RAN1#124 | 9.3.2.1 | Agreement | Capture the following in TR 38.769 on periodic synchronization signal and aperiodic synchronization signal.<br>--<br>At least for the functionality of initial frequency synchronization (including frequency acquisition) and initial timing synchronization, source [R1-10321-123-3, vivo], [R1-10321-123-5, CMCC], [R1-10321-123-6, Huawei], [R1-10321-123-9, CATT], [R1-10321-123-11, Xiaomi], [R1-10321-123-14, ZTE], [R1-10321-123-15, Transsion], [R1-10321-123-16, LGE], [R1-10321-123-17, Panasonic], [R1-10321-123-19, Apple], [R1-10321-123-21, MTK], [R1-10321-123-23, Quectel], [R1-10321-123-24, Qualcomm], [R1-10321-123-25, Docomo], [R1-10321-123-28, CEWiT] , [R1-10321-123-7, Ericsson] and [R1-10321-123-28, Sequans] state that the periodic sync signal is needed, following details are stated by companies<br>- Sources [R1-10321-123-3, vivo] and [R1-10321-123-6, Huawei] report that the synchronization signal allows the device to acquire the frequency in which the reader is intending to transmit, and thereby attains coarse frequency synchronization. [R1-10321-123-6, Huawei], and [R1-10321-123-16, LGE] state that periodic sync signal ensures that the device can perform time and frequency synchronization periodically in order to be able to access the network in a timely manner.<br>- Source [R1-10321-123-7, Ericsson] state that the sync-signal should be strictly periodic because new devices can attempt to access the reader anytime, therefore it is an unpredictable event that requires a synchronization signal to be transmitted periodically as to deal with this non-deterministic event.<br>- Sources [R1-10321-123-3, vivo], [R1-10321-123-11, Xiaomi], [R1-10321-123-14, ZTE] and [R1-10321-123-19, Apple] states that periodic sync signal is needed to determine time domain resource for DOA transmission. Sources [R1-10321-123-5, CMCC], [R1-10321-123-21, MTK], [R1-10321-123-14, ZTE], [R1-10321-123-23, Quectel], [R1-10321-123-24, Qualcomm], [R1-10321-123-28, CEWiT] and [R1-10321-123-28, Sequans] states that periodic sync signal is needed to for time and frequency synchronization before DOA transmission.<br>- Sources [R1-10321-123-3, vivo], [R1-10321-123-5, CMCC] and [R1-10321-123-6, Huawei] states that, with timing alignment between reader and AIoT device achieved through periodic sync signal, DRX monitoring can be performed.<br>- Sources [R1-10321-123-3, vivo] and [R1-10321-123-25, Docomo] states that, periodic sync signal is needed for AIoT device to obtain broadcast information to access to reader within certain duration.<br>- Sources [R1-10321-123-9, CATT] and [R1-10321-123-17, Panasonic] states that, both periodic and aperiodic R2D synchronization signals could be supported with the presumption that the A-IoT devices do not require to maintain synchronization with the reader.<br>- Source [R1-10321-123-24, Qualcomm] states that additional periodic sync signal can be configured which is associated with D2R transmission.<br>Following views on aperiodic synchronization signals are provided<br>[Postivie views]<br>- Source [R1-10321-123-16, LGE] state that aperiodic synchronization signal, selectively skipping some of the configured periodic signal is beneficial in terms of resource utilization and reader power consumption, and aperiodic synchronization signal can be considered with periodic synchronization signal as baseline.<br>- Source [R1-10321-123-19, Apple] state that, aperiodic synchronization signal can be additionally supported for reader-triggered scenarios, with periodic synchronization signal as baseline.<br>- Source [R1-10321-123-23, Quectel] state that the aperiodic sync signal is request by AIoT device, and aperiodic synchronization signal can be considered as lower priority.<br>- Source [ZTE] state that aperiodic R2D synchronization signal can also be considered to increase the synchronization accuracy for DO-A traffic transmission.<br>- Source [CATT] and [Panasonic] state that both periodic and aperiodic R2D synchronization signals could be supported with the presumption that the A-IoT devices do not require to maintain synchronization with the reader in Rel-20 to support A-IoT device synchronization to the reader.<br>[Negative views]<br>- Source [R1-10321-123-6, Huawei] state that, with the aperiodic synchronization signal, the device can only perform the timing synchronization and maintain timing tracking at a specific time range. If the device fails to detect the synchronization signal at this time range, then it will fail to access to the network.<br>- Sources [R1-10321-123-3, vivo] and [R1-10321-123-5, CMCC] state that, if the synchronization signal is aperiodic, or there is no default assumption of a periodicity from a device perspective to monitor the synchronization signal, a device has to keep monitoring, which is not feasible for Device 2b/C with limited energy storage.<br>[End of TP]<br>--- | [Chair notes RAN1#124 - eom_03](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124%20-%20eom_03.docx)<br>[R1-2600490](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Docs/R1-2600490.zip) |

| RAN1#124bis | 9.3.1 | Agreement | For R2D periodic transmission of broadcast information, the time resource of a broadcast information transmission is to be selected from the followings<br>- For single-step acquisition (if supported),<br>  - Option B1: immediately after a R2D periodic sync signal transmission<br>  - Option B2: after a R2D periodic sync signal transmission and a pre-defined time<br>    - FFS: details regarding the pre-defined time<br>- For two-step acquisition (if supported),<br>  - For MIB-like broadcast information,<br>    - Option M1: immediately after a periodic R2D sync signal transmission<br>    - Option M2: after a periodic R2D sync signal transmission and a pre-defined time<br>      - FFS: details regarding the pre-defined time<br>  - For SIB1-like broadcast information,<br>    - Option S1: explicitly indicated or derived from the indication in MIB-like broadcast information<br>    - Option S2: pre-defined in relation to the time resource of MIB-like broadcast information | [Chair notes RAN1#124bis_eom5](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124b/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124bis_eom5.docx)<br>[R1-2602283](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124b/Docs/R1-2602283.zip) |
| RAN1#124bis | 9.3.1 | Agreement | For R2D periodic transmission of broadcast information, at least the following transmission parameters for broadcast information are included<br>- For single-step acquisition (if supported),<br>  - Alt1: there is no L1 R2D control information preceding the transmission of broadcast information (if supported)<br>    - M value is a pre-defined value as M=2<br>    - FEC code rate of periodic broadcast information is a pre-defined value<br>    - Repetition number of periodic broadcast information is a pre-defined value<br>  - Alt2: there is L1 R2D control information preceding the transmission of broadcast information (if supported)<br>    - M value, FEC code rate and repetition number are indicated by the L1 R2D control information<br>- For two-step acquisition (if supported),<br>  - For MIB-like broadcast information, there is no L1 R2D control information preceding the transmission of MIB-like broadcast information<br>    - M value is a pre-defined value as M=2<br>    - FEC code rate of periodic broadcast information is a pre-defined value<br>    - Repetition number of periodic broadcast information is a pre-defined value<br>  - For SIB1-like broadcast information, M value, FEC code rate and repetition number<br>    - Option 1: are same as MIB-like broadcast information, and there is no L1 R2D control information preceding the transmission of SIB1-like broadcast information<br>    - Option 2: indicated by L1 R2D control information preceding the transmission of SIB1-like broadcast information<br>    - Option 3: indicated by MIB-like broadcast information, and there is no L1 R2D control information preceding the transmission of SIB1-like broadcast information | [Chair notes RAN1#124bis_eom5](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124b/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124bis_eom5.docx)<br>[R1-2602283](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124b/Docs/R1-2602283.zip) |
| RAN1#124bis | 9.3.1 | Agreement | For R2D periodic sync signal,<br>- Binary sequence type<br>  - Option 1: m-sequence<br>  - Option 2: Golay sequence<br>- A pre-defined sequence length is in the range from [15 or 31 or 127] to 512<br>  - FFS: detail value<br>  - Note: the value of sequence length refers to the original sequence length with no Manchester coding<br>  - Companies are encouraged to investigate achievable MDR of up to 1% for FAR of up to {1, 10}%<br>- A pre-defined chip length is corresponding to M=2<br>- The number of binary sequence(s) is<br>  - Option 1: 1<br>  - Option 2: one value from {2, 3, 4}<br>- FFS: Whether Manchester coding is applied to binary sequence<br>  - Companies are encouraged to compare performance between with and without Manchester coding under same total transmission time duration | [Chair notes RAN1#124bis_eom5](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124b/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124bis_eom5.docx)<br>[R1-2602283](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124b/Docs/R1-2602283.zip) |
| RAN1#124bis | 9.3.1 | Agreement | For chip duration determination of the L1 R2D control information, RAN1 select from the following options:<br>- Option 1: Fixed chip duration. No use of CAP for chip duration determination.<br>- Option 4: Use a set of different binary sequences with fixed or variable length<br>  - Alt.4-1: using binary sequences for SIP. No use of CAP for chip duration determination.<br>  - Alt.4-2: using binary sequences for CAP<br>- Option 5: Use periodic broadcast information to indicate the chip duration | [Chair notes RAN1#124bis_eom5](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124b/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124bis_eom5.docx)<br>[R1-2602284](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124b/Docs/R1-2602284.zip) |
| RAN1#124bis | 9.3.1 | Agreement | For R2D, support that unmodulated sinusoid single tone CFO calibration signal is transmitted both periodically and as needed (aperiodically) | [Chair notes RAN1#124bis_eom5](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124b/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124bis_eom5.docx)<br>[R1-2602284](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124b/Docs/R1-2602284.zip) |
| RAN1#124bis | 9.3.1 | Agreement | For R2D, for the transmission of periodic unmodulated sinusoid single tone CFO calibration signal<br>- The periodicity is to be selected from the followings<br>  - Option 1: same as the pre-defined transmission periodicity (Psync) of R2D periodic sync signal<br>  - Option 2: integer multiple of Psync<br>- The time location is to be selected from the followings<br>  - Option 4-2: after a periodic R2D sync signal transmission<br>    - Alt1: immediately after the periodic R2D sync signal transmission including padding if any<br>    - Alt2: a gap between the periodic R2D sync signal transmission including padding if any and the CFO calibration signal<br>  - Option 5-2: after a periodic broadcast information transmission(s)<br>    - Alt1: immediately after the periodic broadcast information transmission(s) including padding if any<br>    - Alt2: a gap between the periodic broadcast information transmission including padding if any and the CFO calibration signal | [Chair notes RAN1#124bis_eom5](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124b/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124bis_eom5.docx)<br>[R1-2602284](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124b/Docs/R1-2602284.zip) |
| RAN1#124bis | 9.3.1 | Agreement | For R2D, for the transmission of as needed (aperiodic) unmodulated sinusoid single tone CFO calibration signal<br>- The time location is to be selected from the followings<br>  - Option 1: preceding the L1 R2D control information<br>  - Option 2-2: after the data payload of PRDCH at the end of a R2D transmission<br>    - Alt1: immediately after the data payload of PRDCH at the end of a R2D transmission (including padding if any)<br>    - Alt2: a gap between the data payload of PRDCH at the end of a R2D transmission (including padding if any) and the CFO calibration signal<br>  - Option 3: prior to a D2R transmission | [Chair notes RAN1#124bis_eom5](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124b/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124bis_eom5.docx)<br>[R1-2602284](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124b/Docs/R1-2602284.zip) |
| RAN1#124bis | 9.3.1 | Working Assumption | For R2D, device assumes that the frequency location of the unmodulated sinusoid single tone CFO calibration signal transmission is within the frequency resource used for the periodic synchronization signal transmission<br>- FFS: detail frequency location | [Chair notes RAN1#124bis_eom5](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124b/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124bis_eom5.docx)<br>[R1-2602285](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124b/Docs/R1-2602285.zip) |

| RAN1#124bis | 9.3.1 | Agreement | For R2D sequence-based SIP,<br>- Binary sequence type<br>  - Option 1: m-sequence<br>  - Option 2: Golay sequence<br>- Pre-defined sequence length(s) in the range from [7 or 15 or 31 or 127] to 512<br>  - Option 1: single length<br>  - Option 2: multiple lengths<br>  - Note: the value of sequence length refers to the original sequence length with no Manchester coding<br>  - Companies are encouraged to investigate achievable MDR of up to 1% for FAR of up to {1, 10}%<br>- Chip length is<br>  - Option 1: pre-defined and corresponding to M=2<br>  - Option 2: determined from multiple M values<br>    - FFS: how to determine<br>- The number of binary sequence(s)<br>  - Option 1: single sequence for a given length<br>  - Option 2: multiple sequences for a given length<br>- FFS: Whether Manchester coding is applied to binary sequence<br>  - Companies are encouraged to compare performance between with and without Manchester coding under same total transmission time duration | [Chair notes RAN1#124bis_eom5](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124b/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124bis_eom5.docx)<br>[R1-2602285](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124b/Docs/R1-2602285.zip) |
| RAN1#124bis | 9.3.1 | Agreement | For L1 R2D control information, in addition to chip duration, at least the following transmission parameters for L1 R2D control information are to be determined<br>- For the L1 R2D control information preceding data payload in PRDCH<br>  - Option 1: FEC code rate and repetition number are indicated in periodic broadcast information<br>  - Option 2: FEC code rate is a pre-defined value and repetition number is indicated in periodic broadcast information<br>  - Option 3: repetition number is a pre-defined value and FEC code rate is indicated in periodic broadcast information<br>  - FFS: whether paging can be used to update the transmission parameters or not<br>- For the L1 R2D control information preceding broadcast information in the single-step acquisition (if supported)<br>  - FEC code rate of the L1 R2D control information is a pre-defined value<br>  - Repetition number of the L1 R2D control information is a pre-defined value<br>- For the L1 R2D control information preceding SIB1-like broadcast information in the two-step acquisition (if supported)<br>  - Option 1: FEC code rate and repetition number of the L1 R2D control information are indicated in the MIB-like broadcast information<br>  - Option 2: FEC code rate is a pre-defined value and repetition number is indicated in MIB-like broadcast information<br>  - Option 3: Repetition number is a pre-defined value and FEC code rate is indicated in MIB-like broadcast information<br>  - Option 4: FEC code rate is a pre-defined value and repetition number is a pre-defined value | [Chair notes RAN1#124bis_eom5](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124b/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124bis_eom5.docx)<br>[R1-2603435](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124b/Docs/R1-2603435.zip) |

| RAN1#124bis | 9.3.1 | Agreement | For R2D, for interleaving for PRDCH with FEC, RAN1 further select one from the followings:<br>- Alt 1: reuse both LTE sub-block interleaver and LTE bit collection scheme<br>- Alt 2: reuse LTE bit collection scheme without LTE sub-block interleaver<br>- Alt 3: based on LTE bit collection scheme with some update (e.g., for memory reduction) without LTE sub-block interleaver<br>  - Each sub-block is divided into one or two segments according to TB size. | RAN1#125 | 9.3.1 | Agreement | If two-step acquisition is supported, previous agreement is updated as below for two-step acquisition.<br>\| For R2D, for the transmission of periodic unmodulated sinusoid single tone CFO calibration signal The periodicity is to be selected from the followings Option 1: same as the pre-defined transmission periodicity (Psync) of R2D periodic sync signal Option 2: integer multiple of Psync The time location is to be selected from the followings Option 4-2: after a periodic R2D sync signal transmission Alt1: immediately after the periodic R2D sync signal transmission including padding if any Alt2: a gap between the periodic R2D sync signal transmission including padding if any and the CFO calibration signal Option 5-2: after a periodic MIB-like broadcast information transmission(s) Alt1: immediately after the periodic broadcast information transmission(s) including padding if any Alt2: a gap between the periodic broadcast information transmission including padding if any and the CFO calibration signal \| | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>[R1-2603693](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Docs/R1-2603693.zip) |
| RAN1#125 | 9.3.1 | Agreement | For the unmodulated sinusoid single tone CFO calibration signal transmission, the time duration is integer multiple (>=1) of OFDM symbol duration, i.e., the start and the end of the unmodulated sinusoid single tone CFO calibration signal transmission are aligned at the OFDM symbol boundaries,<br>- at least if the end of the periodic R2D sync signal transmission or periodic broadcast information transmission(s) prior to the unmodulated sinusoid single tone CFO calibration signal transmission is aligned at the OFDM symbol boundary<br>- FFS: detail length of the time duration<br>- FFS: whether the time duration includes time gap (if necessary) placed at the start and at the end | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>[R1-2603693](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Docs/R1-2603693.zip) |
| RAN1#125 | 9.3.1 | Agreement | Confirm the working assumption with the following update<br>\| Working assumption: For R2D, device assumes that the frequency location of the unmodulated sinusoid single tone CFO calibration signal transmission is within the frequency resource used for the periodic synchronization signal transmission FFS: detail frequency location The center frequency of CFO calibration signal is on a sync raster which mapped to one subcarrier within the R2D sync signal transmission bandwidth Details design of sync raster is up to RAN4 \| | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>[R1-2603693](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Docs/R1-2603693.zip) |
| RAN1#125 | 9.3.1 | Agreement | For R2D unmodulated sinusoid single tone CFO calibration signal, the waveform generation is selected from the followings<br>- Option 1: DFT-s-OFDM waveform generation is used to generate unmodulated sinusoid single tone CFO calibration signal<br>  - FFS: necessary specification change for DFT-s-OFDM waveform generation from Rel-19<br>- Option 2: Waveform generation is up to implementation which needs to retain subcarrier orthogonality of OFDM symbols<br>  - FFS: how to retain subcarrier orthogonality of OFDM symbols | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>[R1-2603693](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Docs/R1-2603693.zip) |
| RAN1#125 | 9.3.1 | Agreement | Previous agreement is updated with the following update<br>\| Agreement: For R2D, for the transmission of as needed (aperiodic) unmodulated sinusoid single tone CFO calibration signal The time location is to be selected from the followings Option 1: preceding the L1 R2D control information Option 2-2: after the data payload of PRDCH at the end of a R2D transmission Alt1: immediately after the data payload of PRDCH at the end of a R2D transmission (including padding if any) The presence of the CFO calibration signal transmission is indicated by the L1 R2D control information preceding the payload of PRDCH Alt2: a gap between the data payload of PRDCH at the end of a R2D transmission (including padding if any) and the CFO calibration signal Option 3: prior to a D2R transmission \| | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>[R1-2603693](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Docs/R1-2603693.zip) |
| RAN1#125 | 9.3.1 | Agreement | For sequence-based SIP, multiple pre-defined sequence lengths are to be selected in the range from 31 to 511 | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>[R1-2603694](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Docs/R1-2603694.zip) |
| RAN1#125 | 9.3.1 | Agreement | For sequence-based SIP, the number of sequences for a given length is<br>- Option 1: Single sequence for a given length<br>- Option 2: At least 3 sequences for a given length<br>- Note: For the selection of the number of sequence(s) for a given length, both the sequence correlation performance and the performance of the following PRDCH transmission (including L1 control information and subsequent data payload) are considered under the same interference assumptions from multiple readers. | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>[R1-2603694](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Docs/R1-2603694.zip) |
| RAN1#125 | 9.3.1 | Agreement | For R2D, for interleaving for PRDCH with FEC, Alt1 is supported.<br>- Alt 1: reuse both LTE sub-block interleaver and LTE bit collection scheme | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>[R1-2603694](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Docs/R1-2603694.zip) |
| RAN1#125 | 9.3.1 | Agreement | L1 R2D control information and the subsequent scheduled data payload are included in the same PRDCH<br>- If repetitions applied, L1 R2D control information and the scheduled data payload are repeated separately within the PRDCH (i.e., repetition of L1 R2D control information followed by repetition of scheduled data)<br>- L1 R2D control information (including padding if any) and the scheduled data payload (including padding if any) are contiguous in time | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>[R1-2603694](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Docs/R1-2603694.zip) |
| RAN1#125 | 9.3.1 | Agreement | Previous agreement is updated as below.<br>\| For L1 R2D control information, in addition to chip duration, at least the following transmission parameters for L1 R2D control information are to be determined For the L1 R2D control information preceding data payload in PRDCH Option 1: FEC code rate and repetition number are indicated in periodic broadcast information Option 2: FEC code rate is a pre-defined value and repetition number is indicated in periodic broadcast information Option 3: repetition number is a pre-defined value and FEC code rate is indicated in periodic broadcast information FFS: whether paging can be used to update the transmission parameters or not For the L1 R2D control information preceding broadcast information in the single-step acquisition (if supported) FEC code rate of the L1 R2D control information is a pre-defined value Repetition number of the L1 R2D control information is a pre-defined value For the L1 R2D control information preceding SIB1-like broadcast information in the two-step acquisition (if supported) Option 1: FEC code rate and repetition number of the L1 R2D control information are indicated in the MIB-like broadcast information Option 2: FEC code rate is a pre-defined value and repetition number is indicated in MIB-like broadcast information Option 3: Repetition number is a pre-defined value and FEC code rate is indicated in MIB-like broadcast information Option 4: FEC code rate is a pre-defined value and repetition number is a pre-defined value \| | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>[R1-2603694](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Docs/R1-2603694.zip) |
| RAN1#125 | 9.3.1 | Agreement | For R2D periodic sync signal, if number of sequences for R2D periodic sync signal is 1, Manchester coding is applied to binary sequence | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>[R1-2603694](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Docs/R1-2603694.zip) |
| RAN1#125 | 9.3.1 | Agreement | From device perspective, for the reception of non-periodic R2D transmission, RAN1 select from the following options for potential collision handling with periodic R2D transmission<br>- Option 1: Device assumes non-periodic R2D transmission does not collide with periodic R2D transmission<br>- Option 2: Device assumes non-periodic R2D transmission is postponed if any part of the non-periodic R2D transmission collides with periodic R2D transmission<br>  - Note: Device assumes to also receive the periodic transmission<br>  - FFS: Only the collision part and the followings of non-periodic R2D transmission is postponed or the whole non-periodic R2D transmission is postponed<br>- Option 2a: Device assumes the collision part of non-periodic R2D transmission is dropped if it collides with periodic R2D transmission<br>  - Note: Device assumes to also receive the periodic transmission<br>  - FFS: performance impact on non-periodic R2D transmission<br>- Option 2b: Device assumes at least the collision part of non-periodic R2D transmission is dropped if it collides with periodic R2D transmission<br>  - Note: Device assumes to also receive the periodic transmission<br>  - FFS: performance impact on non-periodic R2D transmission<br>- Option 3: Device assumes to receive non-periodic R2D transmission if it collides with periodic R2D transmission, and at least the collision part of the periodic R2D transmission is dropped<br>  - FFS: Impact to other devices which assume to receive the dropped periodic R2D transmission<br>- Option 4: If non-periodic R2D transmission collides with periodic R2D transmission, it is up to device implementation which to receive<br>  - Note: It implies the Reader can transmit either of periodic R2D transmission or non-periodic R2D transmission<br>  - FFS: Impact to other devices which assume to receive the dropped periodic R2D transmission<br>- Note: It does not preclude that above different options may apply to different collision cases if any needed | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>[R1-2603694](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Docs/R1-2603694.zip) |

No use of CAP for chip duration determination.<br>  - Alt.4-2: using binary sequences for CAP<br>- Option 5: Use periodic broadcast information to indicate the chip duration | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>[R1-2603694](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Docs/R1-2603694.zip) |

| RAN1#126 | 9.3.1 | Agreement | For L1 R2D control information preceding periodic broadcast information (if supported), at least the following contents are included<br>- TBS of subsequent periodic broadcast information payload<br>- Transmission parameters for subsequent periodic broadcast information<br>  - FEC, repetition and chip duration (M value)<br>    - FFS: Whether separate or joint indication is needed<br>- FFS: other contents, e.g.,<br>  - [Presence of aperiodic CFO calibration signal after the data payload]<br>  - [(part of) Physical layer Reader ID]<br>  - [Message type]<br>  - [Time duration of CFO calibration signal]<br>- FFS: Content structure and payload size | [Chair notes RAN1#126_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126_eom1.docx)<br>[R1-2605362](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Docs/R1-2605362.zip) |

| RAN1#126 | 9.3.1 | Agreement | For R2D periodic transmission of broadcast information, RAN1 select following design<br>  - The periodic broadcast information is transmitted in two parts<br>  - The first part of broadcast information is transmitted with<br>    - Transmission periodicity: same as Psync<br>    - Time resource: immediately after a R2D periodic sync signal transmission including padding if any<br>    - Transmission parameters: pre-defined<br>    - The content of the first part at least includes<br>      - (part of) physical layer Reader ID<br>      - Transmission parameters of the remaining part<br>      - FFS: other content of the first part<br>      - Note: the content structure of the first part is same between the following cases<br>        - The first part is preceding the remaining part of broadcast information<br>        - The first part is not preceding the remaining part of broadcast information<br>  - The remaining part of broadcast information is transmitted with<br>    - Transmission periodicity: integer multiple (>1) of Psync<br>    - Time resource: immediately after a first part transmission including padding if any<br>    - Transmission parameters: indicated by the first part<br>  - Note: the time location where periodic sinusoid single-tone CFO calibration signal is transmitted can be further discussed | [Chair notes RAN1#126_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126_eom1.docx)<br>[R1-2605363](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Docs/R1-2605363.zip) |
| RAN1#126 | 9.3.1 | Agreement | For L1 R2D control information preceding scheduled data payload, at least the following contents are carried<br>- TBS (same as Rel-19)<br>- Transmission parameters for subsequent data payload<br>  - FEC, repetition and chip duration (M value)<br>    - FFS: Whether separate or joint indication is needed<br>- Presence of aperiodic CFO calibration signal after the data payload<br>- (part of) Physical layer Reader ID<br>- Device ID for device monitoring unicast transmission, or pre-defined ID for device monitoring non-unicast transmission e.g. paging<br>- FFS: other contents, e.g.,<br>  - [Message type]<br>  - [Time duration of CFO calibration signal]<br>- FFS: Content structure and payload size<br>  - Whether some content needs to be carried in CRC mask | [Chair notes RAN1#126_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126_eom1.docx)<br>[R1-2605363](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Docs/R1-2605363.zip) |

| RAN1#126 | 9.3.1 | Agreement | For R2D, for the transmission of periodic unmodulated sinusoid single tone CFO calibration signal<br>- The periodicity is to be selected from the followings<br>  - Option P1: same as the pre-defined transmission periodicity (Psync) of R2D periodic sync signal<br>  - Option P2: integer multiple (>1) of Psync and same as transmission periodicity of the remaining part of broadcast information<br>- The time location(s) is to be selected from the followings<br>  - Option T1: immediately after a periodic R2D sync signal transmission including padding if any<br>  - Option T2: immediately after a first part of periodic broadcast information transmission including padding if any<br>  - Option T3: immediately after a remaining part of periodic broadcast information transmission including padding if any | [Chair notes RAN1#126_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126_eom1.docx)<br>[R1-2605364](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Docs/R1-2605364.zip) |

| RAN1#124 | 9.3.2.2 | Agreement | For the study of 1SB/2SB without small frequency shift (SFS), consider two options and capture following observations.<br>- Option 1) 1SB<br>  - [HW]1SB signal has only one side band, i.e., lower side band or upper side band, on either side of center frequency.<br>  - [Xiaomi] [HW][vivo][IITK][Oppo] described 1SB signal generation methods based on phase shift, i.e., Hilbert transform of 2SB baseband signal and filtering of one side band signal from 2SB signal.<br>  - [vivo] [HW] [ZTE][LGE] reported that filtering method could be challenging since two sides are adjacent to each other and it is hard to realize filter with steep roll off.<br>  - [ZTE] [HW][Oppo][LGE] reported that phase shift method could be challenging because it requires a precise 90-degree phase-shift network, which is non-ideal and highly sensitive to circuit matching and stability.<br>  - [QC] [Samsung] reported that Tx LO re-tuning to different frequency points may require additional LO retuning/stabilization time and/or power, especially when frequent change is needed.<br>  - [ZTE] reported that BLER performance is more sensitive to phase errors and frequency offset.<br>  - [E///][IITK][QC][Apple][Samsung][Xiaomi] reported 1SB is spectrum efficient than 2SB, but it is more complex requiring precise filtering.<br>  - [TCL] reported that single sideband output might require the device to have an I/Q modulator or a filtering mechanism to suppress the image frequency.<br>  - [ID] reported that implementing such a sharp filter for generating 1SB signal would not be practical for AIoT devices.<br>  - [CATT] reported that based on the ability of Device 2b/C, the 1SB modulation should be considered to improve the spectrum utilization.<br>- Option 2) 2SB<br>  - [HW] 2SB signal has two sidebands, i.e., lower sideband and upper sideband, on either side of center frequency.<br>  - [QC] [ZTE] [vivo] [CATT] [DCM] [Xiaomi][IITK] pointed out that the transmission signal bandwidth of 2SB signal is two times that for 1SB signal in transmitting the same number of bits; 2SB has lower spectral efficiency than 1SB.<br>  - [ZTE] reported that 2SB modulation is more tolerant to phase error and CFO, offering relatively more robust demodulation performance, due to its symmetric spectrum structure.<br>  - [QC] [Samsung] reported that Tx LO re-tuning to different frequency points may require additional LO retuning/stabilization time and/or power, especially when frequent change is needed.<br>  - [E///][IITK][QC][Samsung] reported that 2SB is simpler to implement/demodulate, yet requires larger bandwidth resulting lower spectral efficiency compared to 1SB.<br>  - [Apple] reported that 2SB transmission provides optimal balance between implementation complexity and spectral efficiency<br>--- | [Chair notes RAN1#124 - | RAN1#124 | 9.3.2.2 | Agreement | - Capture following companies’ observations on small frequency shift for active devices.<br>- ---<br>- Multiple sources have provided views on sinewave based SFS for Rel-20 in aspects including implementation, LO tuning, relation to 1SB with SFS, etc.<br>- [vivo] reported that, for “2SB without SFS” and “1SB with SFS”, whether to have SFS or not is an implementation issue and 2SB with SFS has the worst spectrum efficiency.<br>- [Spredtrum] reported that SFS followed by up-conversion is more friendly for low complexity and cost devices since it does not need frequent retuning.<br>- [QC] reported that sinewave-based SFS allows device LO tuning to common carrier frequency, whereas devices without sinewave-based SFS should tune to device-specific carrier frequency.<br>- [DCM] reported that 2SB without SFS is feasible.<br>- [Xiaomi] Replacing target frequency fc with (fc-fSFS) in (1SB RF signal without SFS) can generate almost same 1SB RF signal as (1SB RF signal with SFS) but requires lower implementation complexity.<br>- [ASUSTek] reported that the reference frequency can be commonly provided to all targeted A-IoT active devices, e.g., via broadcast information or paging-like R2D message. The small frequency shift can be provided by D2R scheduling information in corresponding R2D transmission.<br>- [Samsung] reported that supporting SFS (especially Rel-20 SFS) may introduce additional signal processing blocks beyond LO re-tuning, potentially increasing device-side complexity. Based on it, we state that, in Rel-20, D2R FDMA is supported only by adjusting the LO frequency (i.e., LO re-tuning).<br>- [NEC] reported that the SFS operation for Rel-19 device is not required for device 2b and C, since the baseband signal can be directly adjusted to the intended frequency by up-conversion.<br>- [LGE] reported that sinewave based SFS is more feasible than without SFS because without SFS method requires frequency retuning and may experience increased CFO.<br>--- | [Chair notes RAN1#124 - eom_03](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124%20-%20eom_03.docx)<br>[R1-2601453](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Docs/R1-2601453.zip) |
