| RAN1#125 | 9.3.3 | Agreement | For initial Reader ID-related information acquisition, Reader ID-related information is contained in<br>- Alt. 1: Only periodic broadcast information<br>  - Alt. 1-1: L1 R2D control information of periodic broadcast information (if supported)<br>  - Alt. 1-2: Data payload of periodic broadcast information<br>- Alt. 2: Periodic sync signal sequences (if multiple sync signal sequences are supported) and periodic broadcast information<br>  - Alt. 2-1: Periodic sync signal sequences and L1 R2D control information of periodic broadcast information (if supported)<br>  - Alt. 2-2: Periodic sync signal sequences and data payload of periodic broadcast information<br>- Note: Whether the periodic broadcast information is MIB-like or SIB1-like is depending on discussion in AI 9.3.1. | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>[R1-2603965](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Docs/R1-2603965.zip) |
| RAN1#125 | 9.3.3 | Agreement | For D2R open-loop power control, down-select from one of the following options:<br>- Option 1: Device calculates Tx power based on measured pathloss, a predefined formula, and some configured parameters from reader.<br>    - PCMAX is the [configured or predefined] maximum device output power to be defined by RAN4.<br>    - MD2R is the D2R transmission bandwidth normalized by the minimum D2R transmission bandwidth<br>      - Note: the D2R transmission bandwidth is 2/Tb from RAN1 perspective.<br>    - P0 is the target Rx power at reader which can be provided by reader<br>      - FFS: whether power ramping is needed and for Msg1 and first D2R transmission for DO-A<br>      - FFS: whether/how to set/adjust P0<br>      - FFS: whether/how to introduce device-specific component in P0<br>    - is coefficient of PL which can be provided by reader<br>      - FFS:  fixed to 1 for Msg1 and first D2R transmission for DO-A<br>    - , where  is provided by reader,  is measured based on at least periodic R2D synchronization signal<br>    - FFS additional parameter, e.g.,<br>    - FFS other conditions<br>- Option 2: Device measures RSRP, and uses a corresponding Tx power when the  falls in an  range.<br>  - is measured based on at least periodic R2D synchronization signal<br>  - The  range is based on  threshold(s) configured or predefined.<br>    - FFS  range(s) and corresponding  threshold(s) and D2R transmission power value(s).<br>      - D2R transmission power value(s) is configured, FFS value(s) | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>[R1-2603966](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Docs/R1-2603966.zip) |
| RAN1#125 | 9.3.3 | Agreement | At least D2R preamble is used for D2R RSRP-like measurement for device localization.<br>- FFS D2R midamble/PDRCH is used for D2R RSRP-like measurement for device localization.<br>- RAN1 assumes D2R RSRP measurement accuracy is to be handled by RAN4. | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>[R1-2603966](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Docs/R1-2603966.zip) |
| RAN1#125 | 9.3.3 | Agreement | For device localization,<br>- For OOK modulation, the D2R RSRP is defined as the linear average over the power contributions (in Watts) of the ON-state chips of preamble [and midamble/PDRCH] over D2R transmission bandwidth.<br>- For BPSK modulation, the D2R RSRP is defined as the linear average over the power contribution (in Watts) of the chips of preamble [and midamble/PDRCH] over D2R transmission bandwidth. | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>[R1-2603966](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Docs/R1-2603966.zip) |
| RAN1#125 | 9.3.3 | Agreement | For device localization RSRP-like measurement, support one of the following options<br>- Option 1: Reader indicates a power value from set of values to device, and device uses the corresponding power for D2R transmission.<br>  - FFS set of values<br>- Option 2: Device reports resulting D2R transmission power based on open loop power control<br>  - FFS details e.g., the D2R transmission power in a quantized value.<br>- Option 3: Reader indicates Device transmits D2R with a pre-defined power value<br>  - FFS the pre-defined value of power e.g., PCMAX. | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>[R1-2603966](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Docs/R1-2603966.zip) |
| RAN1#125 | 9.3.3 | Agreement | For resource allocation for the first D2R transmission for DO-A, down select one from the following options<br>- Option 1: Each D2R resource set contains one resource group<br>  - If RSRP threshold(s) for the RSRP range(s) is provided by a periodic broadcast information, the resource group is associated with a RSRP range<br>  - Note: If a D2R resource set contains one resource group, the resource group and the resource set are same<br>- Option 2: Each D2R resource set contains one or multiple D2R resource group(s)<br>  - If RSRP threshold(s) for the RSRP range(s) is provided by a periodic broadcast information, each resource group is associated with a RSRP range | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>[R1-2603967](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Docs/R1-2603967.zip) |

| RAN1#125 | 9.3.3 | Agreement | For simultaneous operation or collision handling between Uu and A-IoT at intermediate UE in D2T2, consider the following cases<br>- Case 1: Simultaneous Rx of Uu DL and Rx of A-IoT D2R<br>- Case 2: Simultaneous Tx of Uu UL and Tx of A-IoT R2D<br>- Case 3: Simultaneous Tx of Uu UL and Rx of A-IoT D2R<br>- Case 4: Simultaneous Rx of Uu DL and Tx of A-IoT R2D<br>For the cases above, study at least<br>- whether collision handling solution is needed, if intermediate UE is not capable of simultaneous operation.<br>- whether a solution is needed, if intermediate UE is capable of simultaneous transmission of Uu UL and A-IoT R2D but the total UE transmission power would exceed PCMAX. | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>[R1-2605112](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Docs/R1-2605112.zip) |
| RAN1#125 | 9.3.3 | Agreement | Following update on previous agreement is made for further analysis.<br>\| Agreement: RAN1#124bis To provide the necessary information (i.e., resource allocation related information) for the first D2R transmission for DO-A to start DO-A traffic transmission, support at least one of the following options: Option 1: The first D2R transmission for DO-A is Msg1-like content, and the necessary information is provided by periodic broadcast information. In Option 1, the assumption is that the CBRA access procedure is used as defined by RAN2 Option 3: The first D2R transmission for DO-A is DO-A scheduling request, and the necessary information is provided by periodic broadcast information. FFS: details of scheduling request In Option 3, the assumption is that after the scheduling request, the CBRA access procedure is used as defined by RAN2 FFS: other assumption Note: how to provide the necessary information (i.e., resource allocation related information) for the subsequent D2R transmission for DO-A after the first D2R transmission for DO-A will be discussed Consider at least following aspects for above options (including combination) Traffic type (periodic, event-triggered) System/Signaling/resource overhead, including how resource is configured/provided, what the content size assumption is, what is the structure of first D2R transmission is, etc. Latency \| | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>[R1-2605112](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Docs/R1-2605112.zip) |
| RAN1#126 | 9.3.3 | Agreement | Regarding timing related information to be included in periodic broadcast information, support introducing broadcast information index.<br>- For single-step broadcast information acquisition (if supported),<br>  - Alt.1) the broadcast information index is included in L1 control of the broadcast information (if supported)<br>  - Alt.2) the broadcast information index is included in data payload of the broadcast information.<br>  - Alt.3) part of the broadcast information index is included in the L1 control of the broadcast information (if supported) and the remaining part in the data payload of the broadcast information<br>- For two-step broadcast information acquisition (if supported),<br>  - Alt.1) the broadcast information index is included in the MIB-like broadcast information<br>  - Alt.2) the broadcast information index is included in the SIB1-like broadcast information<br>  - Alt.3) part of the broadcast information index is included in the MIB-like broadcast information and the remaining part in the SIB1-like broadcast information<br>- FFS: value range of the index<br>- FFS: when/how to use the timing related information as timing reference for subsequent R2D/D2R transmissions | [Chair notes RAN1#126_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126_eom1.docx)<br>[R1-2606198](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Docs/R1-2606198.zip) |

| RAN1#123 | 10.6.1 | Agreement | For the evaluation of GNSS resilient NR-NTN operation, consider the following solutions at least for initial access procedure at least to increase PRACH tolerance and/or reducing time/frequency uncertainty:<br>- Solution 1A: Multiple PRACH transmissions (e.g. with different roots or different formats or with different time/frequency pre-compensation using multiple reference locations within the uncertainty area) using existing PRACH formats<br>- Solution 1B: New PRACH restricted sets.<br>- Solution 1C: Single PRACH transmission with multiple TAC/FAC commands in single/multiple RAR MAC PDU scheduling multiple msg3 with different TA/FA.<br>- Solution 1D: Signalling enhancements for Msg2/Msg4 (e.g. enhanced TA command, frequency adjustment command, reference point adjustment command).<br>- Solution 1E: configuration/selection of a set of existing PRACH root for a Single PRACH transmission.<br>- Solution 1F: PRACH transmission using TA margin indicated by Network and RO masking.<br>- Solution 1G: Adaptation of PRACH configuration.<br>- Solution 2A: Single/multi-satellite DL-TDOA based on current specifications.<br>- Solution 2B: Multiple random access attempts based on different time/frequency pre-compensation hypotheses (e.g. based on multiple reference points within the uncertainty area)<br>- Solution 2C: Solutions based on broadcasting DL timestamp(s).<br>- Solution 2D: UE side time/frequency pre-compensation based on reference location or TA/Doppler compensation information provided by gNB.<br>- Solution 2E: service link time/frequency pre-compensation based on last acquired GNSS position<br>- Solution 2F: UE side time/frequency pre-compensation based on reference signal.<br>- Solution 3: Implementation-based techniques e.g. using a long enough PRACH processing window and multiple timing hypotheses for PRACH preamble reception with large max differential delay.<br>Other Solutions are not precluded.<br>As part of the evaluation of the solutions above, at least the following aspects should be assessed:<br>- specification impact when relevant (including whether the solutions remain within the scope of the SID)<br>- performance,<br>- applicability to different scenarios,<br>- complexity,<br>- Coexistence with legacy UEs<br>- the signalling overhead. | [Chair notes RAN1#123 - eom3](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_123/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23123%20-%20eom3.docx)<br>[R1-2508469](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_123/Docs/R1-2508469.zip) |

| RAN1#124 | 9.6.1 | Agreement | For the evaluation of GNSS resilient NR-NTN operation at least for initial access, the companies are encouraged to further study the following candidate solutions<br>- Solution 2D: UE side time/frequency pre-compensation based on reference location or TA/Doppler compensation information provided by gNB.<br>- Solution 1D: Signalling enhancements for Msg2/Msg4 (e.g. enhanced TA command, frequency adjustment command, reference point adjustment command).<br>- Solution 2E: service link time/frequency UE side pre-compensation based on last acquired GNSS position<br>- Solution 1A: Multiple PRACH transmissions (e.g. with different roots or cyclic shifts or different formats or with different time/frequency pre-compensation using multiple reference locations within the uncertainty area) using existing PRACH formats<br>- Solution 2A: Single/multi-satellite DL-TDOA based on current specifications.<br>- Solution 3: Implementation-based techniques e.g. using a long enough PRACH processing window and multiple timing hypotheses for PRACH preamble reception with large max differential delay.<br>- Solution 2B: Multiple random access attempts based on different time/frequency pre-compensation hypotheses (e.g. based on multiple reference points within the uncertainty area)<br>- Solution 1G: Adaptation of PRACH configuration.<br>- Solution 2C: Solutions based on broadcasting DL timestamp(s).<br>To ensure a good consolidation of the results, companies are encouraged to continue evaluating each solution and their combinations in more detail, in particular with respect to the specification impact where relevant (including whether the solutions remain within the scope of the SID), performance, applicability to different scenarios, complexity, coexistence with legacy UEs, and signalling overhead. | [Chair notes RAN1#124 - eom_03](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124%20-%20eom_03.docx)<br>[R1-2600252](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Docs/R1-2600252.zip) |

| RAN1#124bis | 9.5.1 | Agreement | For the study on GNSS resilient NR-NTN operation, regarding connected mode, at least the following candidate solutions and their combination should be evaluated:<br>- Open-loop time and frequency pre-compensation based on one or more of the following:<br>  - Available and/or applicable assistance information provided by network<br>  - UE location information available at UE<br>  - Satellite ephemeris<br>  - Note: Assistance information provided by network and UE location information available at UE used based on solutions for initial access can be used for connected mode.<br>- TA control, including:<br>  - reuse of legacy closed-loop TA;<br>  - study of enhancements such as extended TAC range, TA drift.<br>- New explicit FAC for connected mode, including:<br>  - explicit indication of instantaneous and/or relative frequency offset;<br>  - possible support of accumulated correction and, if needed, study of optional drift-related parameters.<br>- Overhead and robustness optimization, including:<br>  - combined TAC and FAC indication;<br>  - study of mechanisms to reduce signaling overhead and improve robustness, while noting that group/common adjustment commands require further assessment due to mixed support.<br>- UE reference location update for connected mode (e.g. based on explicit PAC for connected mode)<br>As part of the evaluation of the candidate solutions above, RAN1 should assess at least:<br>- performance, including timing/frequency accuracy and signaling overhead;<br>- applicability to different scenarios, including different orbit types, mobility conditions, cell types, and GNSS outage assumptions;<br>- complexity;<br>- specification impact, including whether the solution remains within the scope of the SID. | [Chair notes RAN1#124bis_eom5](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124b/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124bis_eom5.docx) |

| RAN1#125 | 9.5.1 | Agreement | For GNSS resilient NR-NTN operation for Connected Mode, the following mechanisms are recommended.<br>- Open-loop time and frequency pre-compensation based on one or more of the following:<br>- Assistance information provided by network<br>  - At least reference location is recommended for Earth fixed cell<br>- UE location information available at UE<br>- Satellite ephemeris<br>- Note: Assistance information provided by network  and UE location information available at UE used based on solutions for initial access can be used for connected mode.<br>- TA control, including:<br>- Reuse of legacy closed-loop TA for NTN;<br>- New explicit FAC (frequency adjustment command) for connected mode<br>- Implicit (based on FAC) or explicit compensation for TA drift<br>Additional enhancements (e.g. Overhead and robustness optimization, and UE reference location update) are not precluded, if justified. | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>[R1-2603742](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Docs/R1-2603742.zip) |

If such design constraint had not been there, the recommendation above might have been different. | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>[R1-2603744](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Docs/R1-2603744.zip) |

| RAN1#125 | 9.6.1 | Agreement | With respect to RAN2 LS (R1-2603484), the following is endorsed for response.<br>Conclusion for UL SPS with multi-TBS (after offline):<br>Introducing a multiple-TB-size mechanism in a similar way as defined for Rel-15 EDT (e.g., edt-SmallTBS-Enabled) for UL SPS for NB-IoT NTN could be beneficial for UE power saving and reducing the impact of power backoff due to SAR requirements, if the transmission repetition number for a UE-selected smaller TBS is smaller than that of the configured TBS. However, it requires blind decoding at the network side, and it is challenging to reuse the unused resources after UE selecting a smaller TBS for another UE.<br>While it may be technically feasible to support this mechanism for UL SPS for NB-IoT NTN, it may be challenging to implement this mechanism at network side. There is also no RAN1 consensus on the potential RAN1 specification impacts at this stage, and RAN1 considers this mechanism as not feasible given that the limited TUs allocated.<br>The draft LS in R1-2605096 is endorsed. The final LS in R1-2605105. | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>[R1-2603637](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Docs/R1-2603637.zip) |

| RAN1#122 | 10.2.2 | Agreement | For a UE transition from IDLE to CONNECTED mode, support the following procedure at least for early aperiodic SRS-AS/CSI-RS/CSI triggering (i.e., early triggering of aperiodic SRS-AS transmission, aperiodic CSI-RS reception, aperiodic CSI reporting):<br>- Step-1: The UE receives the resource/reporting configuration(s) for early SRS-AS/CSI-RS/CSI triggering provided in the system information before MSG3.<br>  - FFS: Which SIB is used to carry the resource/reporting configuration(s) for early SRS-AS/CSI/CSI-RS triggering<br>- Step-2: The UE reports its capability on early SRS/CSI-RS/CSI triggering through MSG3<br>- Step-3: The UE receives MSG4 that triggers early SRS-AS/CSI-RS/CSI based on  the capability reported by the UE.<br>- Step-4: The UE performs aperiodic SRS-AS transmission, aperiodic CSI-RS reception, and/or aperiodic CSI reporting.<br>  - FFS: Timeline of the aperiodic SRS-AS transmission, aperiodic CSI-RS reception, aperiodic CSI reporting<br>Note: The term “capability” above does not mean legacy RRC based UE capability.<br>FFS: For a UE transition from INACTIVE to CONNECTED mode, whether above procedure can be reused at least for early aperiodic SRS-AS/CSI-RS/CSI triggering<br>Note: Whether the aperiodic SRS-AS transmission, aperiodic CSI-RS reception, and/or aperiodic CSI reporting can be configured/triggered simultaneously will be discussed separately | [Chair notes RAN1#122 eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_122/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23122%20eom.zip)<br>[R1-2506539](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_122/Docs/R1-2506539.zip) |
| RAN1#122 | 10.2.2 | Agreement | CSI-RS frequency-domain density ρ = 1/4 can be configured to the K NZP CSI-RS resources at least for the following cases:<br>  - K=2 24-port NZP CSI-RS resources in a CSI-RS resource set aggregating 48 CSI-RS ports<br>  - K=4 16-port NZP CSI-RS resources in a CSI-RS resource set aggregating 64 CSI-RS ports<br>  - K=2 32-port NZP CSI-RS resources in a CSI-RS resource set aggregating 64 CSI-RS ports<br>  - K=4 32-port NZP CSI-RS resources in a CSI-RS resource set aggregating 128 CSI-RS ports<br>FFS: K=3 16-port NZP CSI-RS resources in a CSI-RS resource set aggregating 48 CSI-RS ports<br>Note: It’s not precluded that the frequency-domain density configured to the K NZP CSI-RS resources in the same CSI-RS resource set for 48/64/128 CSI-RS ports aggregation can be different | [Chair notes RAN1#122 eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_122/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23122%20eom.zip)<br>[R1-2506539](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_122/Docs/R1-2506539.zip) |

| RAN1#122 | 10.2.2 | Agreement | For early triggering of SRS-AS/CSI-RS/CSI when UE transition from IDLE to CONNECTED mode, study the following at least three options for Step-1 and Step-2:<br>- Option-1: NW can provide the resource/report configuration in SIBx based on only one UE capability assumption, and UE can report through MSG3 whether the resource/report configuration received in SIBx is supported.<br>- Option-2: NW can provide the resource/report configuration(s) in SIBx based on one or multiple UE capability assumptions, and UE can report through MSG3 which resource/report configuration(s) received in SIBx is/are supported.<br>- Option-3: NW can provide the resource/report configuration(s) in SIBx based on one or multiple UE capability assumptions, and UE can report through MSG3 the supported capability(s) of early SRS/CSI/CSI-RS triggering (e.g., whether to support this feature, max number of CSI-RS ports, xTyR for SRS-AS, max bandwidth of the CSI-RS/SRS-AS etc.).<br>Note: The term “capability” or “UE capability” above does not mean legacy RRC based UE capability. | [Chair notes RAN1#122 eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_122/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23122%20eom.zip)<br>[R1-2506583](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_122/Docs/R1-2506583.zip) |

### 9.3 Study of Enhancements for solutions for Ambient IoT (Internet of Things) in NR outdoor for active devices (마지막: RAN1#124)

회의별 결정 수: #122 0 · #122bis 0 · #123 0 · #124 8 · #124bis 0 · #125 0 · #126 0

| 회의 | 번호 | 구분 | 내용 | 출처 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| RAN1#124 | 9.3 | Agreement | Capture following TP into section 8.2 of TR38.769<br>\| RAN1 defined necessary further evaluation assumptions of deployment scenarios for coverage and coexistence evaluations, as reported in Clause 4.2.2. The link budget calculation for coverage is reported in Clause 4.3.2. The achievable cell edge data rates, the corresponding maximum distances between reader and device, BS/device transmit power for device C/2b, etc., are reported in Clause 7.3. Values between -3 dBm and 5 dBm are feasible maximum transmit power for Device C, from device power consumption perspective. RAN1 observes 5 dBm as the maximum transmit power for Device C to achieve maximum coverage in outdoor scenarios. Values between -3dBm and 5dBm are feasible to achieve different coverage. This does not preclude RAN to select any value(s) between -3 dBm and 5 dBm as maximum transmit power for Device C. Assumptions on the energy harvesting/storage used to obtain the reported data rates, specifically on the energy source and the energy storage capacity, are reported in Clause 4.5. For Device 2b and C, the maximum distance between reader and device, differentiated per pathloss model, BS transmit power, Device transmit power, data rate, penetration margin, BLER, etc. are reported in Clause 7.3. Device C achieves better coverage than Device 2b for both R2D and D2R. Device 2b is applicable to outdoor scenarios for short distance e.g. 50-200m. Device C is applicable to outdoor scenarios for both short and large distance e.g. 50-500m. Necessity of Device 2b and C in terms of aspects other than coverage is up to RAN decision. \| | [Chair notes RAN1#124 - eom_03](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124%20-%20eom_03.docx)<br>[R1-2601624](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Docs/R1-2601624.zip)<br>`[124-R20-A-IoT]` |
| RAN1#124 | 9.3 | Agreement | Capture following TP into section 8.2 of TR38.769<br>\| RAN1 studied and found necessary and feasible changes to the Rel-19 air interface to support A-IoT in outdoor scenarios under the conditions stated in [SID, RP-252964]. Regarding the R2D modulation and waveform, shorter and longer chip durations as compared to the Rel-19 chip durations were studied, with their pros/cons reported by companies. R2D multiplexing using FDMA was also studied. Regarding the changes to the PRDCH in R2D, the necessity and feasibility of introducing FEC, interleaving, bit collection and repetition were presented, and feasible candidates for these enhancements have been compared and documented, as reported by companies. There is no need to remove Manchester coding for Rel-20 A-IoT PRDCH. Necessity and feasibility of R2D scrambling were also studied. The R-TAS was identified as requiring changes to support active device for outdoor scenarios, with a new SIP, where the feasible candidates for the SIP were studied, with the different design aspects identified. Candidate solutions for the device to determine the chip duration of the L1 R2D control information and the data payload of the PRDCH have been studied, with their respective pros/cons identified by company reports. New R2D physical signals including periodic synchronization signal and CFO calibration signal, and periodic transmission of broadcast information have been identified as necessary for the functionalities of initial time/frequency synchronization, CFO estimation/LO calibration at the device and providing necessary information for subsequent transmission and reception, respectively. Candidate solutions for the functionality of SFO calibration were identified, without the need for a new SFO calibration signal. L1 R2D control information with a separate CRC has been studied by company reports, including the aspects of potential content, including the TBS to indicate the end of the PRDCH transmission, time and frequency locations, and transmission parameters (CRC/FEC/repetition/payload size) of the L1 R2D control information. \| | [Chair notes RAN1#124 - eom_03](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124%20-%20eom_03.docx)<br>[R1-2601624](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Docs/R1-2601624.zip)<br>`[124-R20-A-IoT]` |
| RAN1#124 | 9.3 | Agreement | Capture following TP into section 8.2 of TR38.769<br>\| Four D2R modulation schemes, i.e., BPSK/OOK/DBPSK/MSK, have been studied considering their performance, sensitivity to CFO, overhead, complexity, etc. Enhancements on D2R preamble and midamble have been identified, where the sequence type/length/number, insertion interval, etc. were studied. D2R interleaving and bit-collection were studied considering performance gain and required memory. The study assumes single-carrier waveform for D2R. Rel-19 SFS is not necessary in Rel-20 A-IoT D2R. 1SB/2SB without small frequency shift (SFS) were studied considering pros/cons, implementation complexity, etc. For D2R FEC scheme, in addition to 1/3 code rate, both 1/4 and 1/2 were studied considering their performance, complexity, etc. D2R scrambling is necessary for randomizing interference and preventing long runs of identical bits when Manchester code is not applied. For D2R repetition, the introduction of additional number of D2R repetitions larger than 2 was considered. D2R CDM(A), i.e., D2R sequence based Msg1, has been studied, including sequence type/length/number, performance aspects, and potential impact to random access procedures. For CBRA for DT and DO-DTT, enhancements of D2R TDM(A), i.e., X1 > 2 for Msg1, X3 > 1 for Msg3 (X1/X3: number of time domain resources for Msg1/Msg3 transmission indicated by the corresponding R2D message), have been studied. For R2D and D2R, the order of channel coding (including interleaver if supported) and block-level repetition (if supported) for complexity reduction, considering necessity and feasibility, has been studied. \| | [Chair notes RAN1#124 - eom_03](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124%20-%20eom_03.docx)<br>[R1-2601624](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Docs/R1-2601624.zip)<br>`[124-R20-A-IoT]` |
| RAN1#124 | 9.3 | Agreement | Capture following TP into section 8.2 of TR38.769<br>\| Regarding the procedures required to support active devices in outdoor scenarios, both the initial frequency acquisition and reader identification/differentiation procedures have been studied, with the former using the periodic synchronization signal while for the latter, potential candidate solutions on how the device receives the reader ID-related information have been determined. Support for the DO-A traffic type considering both periodic and event-triggered transmissions has been studied, taking into account the time and frequency synchronization required for the device to transmit DO-A traffic, the resource allocation/determination method used, how the necessary information is carried and provided to the device and the subsequent steps the device would need to perform, with candidate solutions for these aspects identified. The necessity of D2R Tx power control for Device 2b and Device C for outdoor scenarios was studied and has majority support, and two methods of open loop power control are identified. Feasibility and necessity of closed-loop power control were also studied. The changes to existing timing offsets, e.g., timing offset value between R2D and corresponding subsequent D2R, etc., have been studied. According to the SID objective, outdoor device localization for Device 2b/Device C has been studied. D2R preamble / D2R midamble / PDRCH is reported as applicable D2R signal(s)/channel(s) for A-IoT device localization. D2R RSRP-like measurement has been studied. Evaluation results along with the device localization methods have also been reported, which achieve more accurate outdoor device localization than based on Reader-ID. \| | [Chair notes RAN1#124 - eom_03](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124%20-%20eom_03.docx)<br>[R1-2601624](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Docs/R1-2601624.zip)<br>`[124-R20-A-IoT]` |
| RAN1#124 | 9.3 | Agreement | Capture following TP into section 8.2 of TR38.769<br>\| According to the SID objective, RAN1 provides following study outcome. At least the following changes to the Rel-19 A-IoT specifications are identified to be feasible and necessary to support outdoor scenario: R2D Periodic R2D sync signal (binary sequence based, with a default pre-defined transmission periodicity) Periodic transmission of broadcast information CFO calibration signal L1 R2D control information with a separate CRC from data (no new R2D physical channel for L1 R2D control information) Chip duration determination for L1 R2D control information Chip duration determination for R2D data payload Binary sequence-based SIP R2D FEC (including LTE bit collection with or without R2D interleaving) and/or block level repetitions for AIoT device in R2D to achieve maximum coverage (e.g., 200 m with penetration loss for Device 2b, 500 m with penetration loss for Device C) as observed in [Refer the TP on Necessity of R2D FEC], and it can be enabled under certain condition No R2D postamble At least the following changes to the Rel-19 A-IoT specifications are identified and may or may not be considered to support outdoor scenario: R2D Addition of M=1 R2D FDM \| | [Chair notes RAN1#124 - eom_03](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124%20-%20eom_03.docx)<br>[R1-2601624](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Docs/R1-2601624.zip)<br>`[124-R20-A-IoT]` |
| RAN1#124 | 9.3 | Agreement | Capture following TP into section 8.2 of TR38.769<br>\| According to the SID objective, RAN1 provides following study outcome. At least the following changes to the Rel-19 A-IoT specifications are identified to be feasible and necessary to support outdoor scenario: D2R Rel-19 SFS is not supported in Rel-20 A-IoT D2R, and support of FDMA without Rel-19 SFS block-level repetitions for D2R for repetition numbers larger than 2 PDRCH scrambling (applied after FEC and repetition, if any) D2R preamble/midamble(s) in terms of at least one of sequence length/number/type, midamble insertion interval, etc. D2R interleaving, and order of FEC and block level repetition At least the following changes to the Rel-19 A-IoT specifications are identified and may or may not be considered to support outdoor scenario: D2R Addition of DBPSK, removal of OOK Additional code rate(s) for D2R FEC (1/2 and/or 1/4) Enhancements on TDMA at least for CBRA for DT and DO-DTT (X1 > 2 for Msg1 and/or X3 > 1 for Msg3) CDMA (sequence-based Msg1 considering sequence type/length/number) \| | [Chair notes RAN1#124 - eom_03](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124%20-%20eom_03.docx)<br>[R1-2601624](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Docs/R1-2601624.zip)<br>`[124-R20-A-IoT]` |
| RAN1#124 | 9.3 | Agreement | Capture following TP into section 8.2 of TR38.769<br>\| According to the SID objective, RAN1 provides following study outcome. Note: SFO after clock calibration can be applied to Fe. | RAN1#122 | 10.5.1 | Agreement | Horizontal/vertical positioning accuracy are agreed as performance metrics for NR ISAC.<br>  - It is defined as the absolute value of the difference between the estimated horizontal/vertical position and the corresponding true position of a sensing target.<br>    - Note: in RAN1 evaluations, there should be only one estimated horizontal/vertical position corresponding to the true position of a sensing target | [Chair notes RAN1#122 eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_122/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23122%20eom.zip)<br>[R1-2506477](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_122/Docs/R1-2506477.zip) |

Horizontal plane: uniformly distributed in a sector Vertical plane: Uniformly distributed between 25m and 300m, optionally distributed between 1.5m and 300m \|<br>\| Mobility \| horizontal speed: uniformly distributed between 0 and 180km/h vertical speed: 0km/h \|<br>Note: N=0 will be discussed in a later proposal in relation to false alarm. | [Chair notes RAN1#122 eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_122/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23122%20eom.zip)<br>[R1-2506478](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_122/Docs/R1-2506478.zip) |
| RAN1#122 | 10.5.1 | Agreement | The following evaluation parameters are agreed for the evaluation on NR ISAC.<br>\| Parameters \| Assumptions \|<br>\| Minimum BS-target 3D distance \| 10 m \|<br>\| Minimum target-target (3D) distance \| 10 m \|<br>\| Target outdoor/indoor proportion \| 100% outdoor \|<br>\| LOS/NLOS \| LOS and NLOS \|<br>\| Orientation \| Random in horizontal domain \|<br>\| RCS model \| RCS model 1 for UAV with small size \| | [Chair notes RAN1#122 eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_122/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23122%20eom.zip)<br>[R1-2506478](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_122/Docs/R1-2506478.zip) |
| RAN1#122 | 10.5.1 | Agreement | For the purpose of performance metric calculation, association of the detected object(s) and the true target(s) should fulfil at least the following conditions:<br>  - One true target is associated with at most one detected object<br>  - One detected object is associated with at most one true target<br>  - The same association applies to miss detection, false alarm probability Type 2 (if defined) and positioning/velocity accuracy<br>  - Companies to report the method used for association of the detected object(s) and the true target(s) | [Chair notes RAN1#122 eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_122/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23122%20eom.zip)<br>[R1-2506479](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_122/Docs/R1-2506479.zip) |
| RAN1#122 | 10.5.1 | Agreement | - Missed detection probability is agreed as performance metric for NR ISAC.<br>  - It is defined as the conditional probability of not detecting the presence of a target when the target is actually present in the simulation area.<br>Where,<br>      - is the number of missed targets in the drop n, i.e., the true target not associated with any detected object<br>      - is the number of true targets in the drop n.<br>      - is total number of drops with at least one target per drop | [Chair notes RAN1#122 eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_122/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23122%20eom.zip)<br>[R1-2506479](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_122/Docs/R1-2506479.zip) |
| RAN1#122 | 10.5.1 | Agreement | - False alarm probability is agreed as performance metric for NR ISAC.<br>  - For cases without true target dropped in simulation area, False alarm probability Type 1 is computed and reported<br>  - For cases with true targets dropped in simulation area, False alarm probability Type 2 is computed and reported<br>  - Note: both False alarm probability Types are mandatory<br>  - KPI values for False alarm probability Type 1 and 2 can be discussed separately.<br>Definitions:<br>  - False alarm probability Type 1 (no target dropped in simulation area): An object is detected when there is no target present in simulation area is considered a false alarm.<br>Where,<br>    - equal to 1 if at least one object is detected when there is no target dropped in the simulation area in the drop n, otherwise  equal to 0.<br>    - is the total number of drops without targets in the simulation area.<br>  - False alarm probability Type 2 (targets dropped in simulation area): An object is detected but not associated with any true targets in the simulation area is considered as a false alarm.<br>Where,<br>      - is the number of detected objects but not associated with any true targets in the drop n.<br>      - is the total number of detected objects in the drop n.<br>      - FFS:<br>        - Option 1:  is number of drops (N)<br>        - Option 2:  is number of drops with at least one detected object<br>Note: the number of targets should be reported by companies when providing False alarm probability Type 2 | [Chair notes RAN1#122 eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_122/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23122%20eom.zip)<br>[R1-2506479](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_122/Docs/R1-2506479.zip) |
| RAN1#122 | 10.5.1 | Agreement | - Velocity accuracy is agreed as performance metric for NR ISAC.<br>  - Velocity accuracy is defined as the absolute value of the difference between the estimated velocity and the corresponding true velocity of a sensing target.<br>  - For single TRP monostatic sensing,<br>    - The radial velocity accuracy can be estimated<br>      - The true radial velocity is the projection of true velocity on the direction from TRP to target for TRP monostatic.<br>    - The true velocity accuracy can be estimated. | [Chair notes RAN1#122 eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_122/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23122%20eom.zip)<br>[R1-2506479](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_122/Docs/R1-2506479.zip) |

| RAN1#122bis | 10.5.1 | Agreement | For the evaluation on NR ISAC,<br>- 3 kinds of resources are defined<br>- Type 1: resources that are used for sensing signal transmission<br>- Type 2: part of Type 1 resources that are used for communication purpose<br>  - Note: it is possible the resource type 2 doesn’t exist<br>- Type 3: resources that are not used for sensing signal transmission, and cannot be used for communication purpose due to sensing operation<br>- Both options should be reported for sensing resource ratio<br>- Option 1: (Type_1 + Type_3) resources over all radio DL and UL resources<br>- Option 2: (Type_1 - Type_2 + Type_3) resources over all radio DL and UL resources<br>- Note: if Type 2 resource doesn’t exist, two options are the same<br>For the evaluation on NR ISAC,<br>- Company should report T/F RE mapping of sensing RS, assumed TDD UL/DL configuration if applicable.<br>- Company should report which sensing RS resources are considered as Type 2 resource and related reason. | [Chair notes RAN1#122b eom4](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_122b/Inbox/Chair_Notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23122b%20eom4.docx)<br>[R1-2507426](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_122b/Docs/R1-2507426.zip) |

| RAN1#123 | 10.5.1 | Agreement | - In section 6.2 Performance evaluation results in TR 38.765,<br>- Multiple configurations of the following parameters are defined to respectively analyze the evaluation results<br>  - At least Two baseline configurations 1 & 2 are defined for evaluation purpose<br>\|  \| Parameters \| Configuration 1 Baseline \| Configuration 2 Baseline \|<br>\| 1 \| Scenario \| (UMa-AV, 500m) \| (UMa-AV, 500m) \|<br>\| 2 \| Sensing Tx/Rx operating simultaneously or not \| Sensing Tx/Rx operating simultaneously \| Sensing Tx/Rx operating simultaneously \|<br>\| 3 \| Carrier frequency \| 4 or 4.9GHz \| 4 or 4.9GHz \|<br>\| 4 \| Max BS Tx power \| 52 dBm \| 37 dBm \|<br>\| 5 \| BS antenna configuration \| (M, N, P, Mg, Ng, Mp, Np) Tx: (8,8,2,1,1;4,8) Rx: (8,8,2,1,1;4,8) = (0.5, 0.8)λ, +45°/-45° polarization \| (M, N, P, Mg, Ng, Mp, Np) Tx: (8,8,2,1,1;4,8) Rx: (8,8,2,1,1;4,8) = (0.5, 0.8)λ, +45°/-45° polarization \|<br>\| 6 \| Number of targets per sector in center site \| N=5 \| N=5 \|<br>\| 7 \| Target vertical distribution \| 25-300m \| 25-300m \|<br>  - Additional configurations can be defined for other assumptions of the parameters, based on reported evaluation results in RAN1 #124. | [Chair notes RAN1#123 - eom3](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_123/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23123%20-%20eom3.docx)<br>[R1-2509238](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_123/Docs/R1-2509238.zip) |

| RAN1#123 | 10.5.1 | Agreement | From RAN1 perspective, the following measurements that may be reported from RAN are identified in the study of NR ISAC. Note: Down selection of Level(s)/Option(s) for recommendation can be discussed separately.<br>- Level A: Raw data per Tx antenna port per OFDM symbol per RX antenna port per TRP for a given time stamp<br>  - Option A1: Amplitude and phase samples in time/delay domain of the estimated channel, i.e., Amplitude and phase values of channel impulse response<br>  - Option A2: Amplitude and phase per subcarrier in frequency domain of the estimated channel<br>- Level B: Amplitude and phase profile of delay, and/or Doppler, and/or angle per TRP for a given time stamp by using window(s) of the [consecutive] samples in delay, Doppler and/or angle domain<br>  - Option B1: Delay-Doppler profile per Tx antenna port per Rx antenna port, which includes the amplitude and phase samples distributed across different delays and Doppler shifts.<br>  - Option B2: Delay-Angle profile per Tx antenna port per OFDM symbol, which includes the amplitude and phase samples distributed across different delays and spatial angles (e.g., Angle of Arrival).<br>  - Option B3: Delay-Doppler-Angle profile per Tx antenna port, which includes the amplitude and phase samples distributed across delay, Doppler, and angle domains.<br>  - Option B4: Delay profile per Tx antenna port per OFDM symbol per Rx antenna port, which includes the amplitude and phase samples distributed across different delays.<br>  - Note: Level B is applicable for either LCS or GCS<br>- Level C: per detected path/point measurements per Tx antenna port per TRP which may be reflected/scattered from scattering point(s).<br>  - Option C1: Delay/range, Doppler/velocity, one or multiple 3D angles, and [power/confidence metric] per detected path for a given time stamp.<br>    - A path is associated with one couple {delay/range, Doppler/velocity, [power/confidence metric]}, and one or multiple 3D angles.<br>  - Option C2: Doppler/velocity, position, and [power/confidence metric] per detected path for a given time stamp.<br>    - A path is associated with one doppler/velocity, [power/confidence metric], one or multiple positions<br>  - Option C3: Delay/range, Doppler/velocity, 3D angle, and [power/confidence metric] per detected path for a given time stamp.<br>    - A path is associated with one delay, and one or multiple triple {Doppler/velocity, 3D angle, [power/confidence metric]}<br>  - Option C4: Delay/range, Doppler/velocity, 3D angle, and [power/confidence metric] per detected point for a given time stamp<br>    - A point is associated with one range/delay, one Doppler/velocity, one 3D angle<br>  - Option C5: Position, velocity, and [power/confidence metric] per detected point for a given time stamp<br>    - A point is associated with one position, one velocity<br>  - FFS: Velocity can be<br>    - Opt 1: radial velocity<br>    - Opt 2: 3D velocity<br>  - Note:<br>    - Position can be defined in either LCS or GCS<br>    - Angle can be defined in either LCS or GCS<br>    - Ambiguity issue will be further discussed<br>    - 3D angle refers to a pair of horizontal and vertical angles<br>- Level D: Object/target level measurement [per TRP or per gNB]<br>  - One or more value pair(s) {position, velocity} in GCS for a given time stamp is reported for a detected object/target,<br>    - Option D1: Only one value pair {position, velocity} in GCS for a given time stamp is reported for a detected object/target. The association of multiple measurements across different time stamps for the same detected object/target is not reported.<br>    - Option D2: Only one value pair {position, velocity} in GCS for a given time stamp is reported for a detected object/target. The association of multiple measurements across different time stamps for the same detected object/target is reported.<br>    - Option D3: One or more value pairs {position, velocity} in GCS for a given time stamp are reported for a detected object/target. The association of multiple measurements across different time stamps for the same detected object/target is reported.<br>    - Option D4: One or more value pairs {position, velocity} in GCS for a given time stamp are reported for a detected object/target. The association of multiple measurements across different time stamps for the same detected object/target is not reported.<br>  - Note: Ambiguity issue can be further discussed if any<br>  - Note: velocity is 3D velocity for Option D2/D3<br>  - FFS: velocity can be radial velocity or 3D velocity for Option D1/D4<br>- Note: the possible information from RAN to SF for further processing can be further discussed for all levels<br>- Note: the possible information from SF to RAN can be further discussed for all levels<br>- Note: confidence metric can be further discussed for options of Level C/D<br>- Note: definition of time stamp for each of all options of all Levels can be further discussed<br>- For Level A/B/C, Tx antenna port means reference signal antenna port for sensing purpose | [Chair notes RAN1#123 - eom3](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_123/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23123%20-%20eom3.docx)<br>[R1-2509241](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_123/Docs/R1-2509241.zip) |

| RAN1#124 | 9.5.1 | Agreement | The payload size estimation of each measurement level/option for NR ISAC can be done by the following formulas<br>- Level A: Msubcarrier* Ncpi *Mtxport*Nrxport*Ntrp*(Nquan1+ Nquan2)<br>Where,<br>  - Msubcarrier: number of subcarriers in a OFDM symbols<br>  - Ncpi: number of OFDM symbols within CPI<br>  - Mtxport: number of reference signal antenna port for sensing purpose<br>  - Nrxport: number of Rx antenna ports<br>  - Ntrp: number of TRPs for payload size calculation<br>  - Nquan1: number of quantized bits for amplitude<br>  - Nquan2: number of quantized bits for angle<br>- Level B:<br>  - Delay-Doppler Profile: Mdelay *Ndoppler *Mtxport* Nrxport *Ntrp *(Nquan1+ Nquan2)<br>  - Delay-angle Profile: Mdelay * Ncpi *Mtxport*Nangle *Ntrp *(Nquan1+ Nquan2)<br>  - Delay-Doppler-angle Profile: Mdelay *Ndoppler *Mtxport*Nangle *Ntrp *(Nquan1+ Nquan2)<br>  - Delay Profile: Mdelay *Ncpi*Mtxport*Nrxport *Ntrp *(Nquan1+ Nquan2)<br>Where,<br>  - Mdelay: number of delay samples in the window<br>  - Ndoppler: number of Doppler samples in the window<br>  - Nangle: number of angle samples in the window<br>- Level C:<br>  - C1/C2/C3: Np1*Ntrp *<br>  - C4/C5: Np2*Ntrp *<br>Where,<br>  - Np1 is total number of paths<br>  - Np2 is total number of points<br>  - Nparam is 5 including e.g.,<br>    - C1/C3/C4: delay, Doppler, horizontal angle, vertical angle, power measurement<br>    - C2/C5: position (x, y, z), radial velocity, power measurement<br>  - Nquan,i: number of quantized bits<br>  - Ntrp: number of TRPs for payload size calculation<br>- Level D:<br>  - Nobject*Ngnb * for options D1/2<br>  - Mpoints* Ngnb * for options D3/4<br>Where,<br>  - Nobject is total number of targets<br>  - Mpoints is total number of scattering points of all targets<br>  - Ngnb is fixed to 1 | [Chair notes RAN1#124 - eom_03](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124%20-%20eom_03.docx)<br>[R1-2601384](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Docs/R1-2601384.zip) |
